It is a Bain Capital Ventures portfolio company in the ai-apps sector. Echelon AI publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, commercial and security surface.

providers.name: Simpplr
providers.description: Simpplr is an AI-powered employee experience platform (modern intranet, employee communications, recognition, and virtual assistant) used by enterprises to inform, engage, and connect their workforce. Built on the Salesforce platform, Simpplr publishes a REST "Extensibility Center" API at developer.simpplr.com that lets developers programmatically manage sites, pages, blogs, events, alerts, notifications, people/audiences, content, search, media, and adoption/engagement analytics. Authentication is OAuth 2.0 (bearer token) via a connected app on the Salesforce platform. Simpplr was founded in 2014, is headquartered in Redwood City, California, and is backed by venture investors including Norwest Venture Partners and Sapphire Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from the VC portfolio pipeline and enriched from Simpplr's public developer surface.

providers.name: Avamar
providers.description: Avamar is enterprise backup and recovery software built on client-side global data deduplication, founded in Irvine, California and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners before EMC acquired the company in November 2006 for approximately $165 million. Avamar now ships as Dell Avamar, part of the Dell Technologies data protection portfolio, and is deployed as a customer-hosted appliance or virtual edition rather than as a public SaaS. It exposes a REST API on the Avamar server for programmatic backup, restore, client, domain, dataset, policy and activity management, secured with OAuth 2.0 access tokens and optional OIDC single sign-on, and documented through a Swagger UI served from the appliance itself. A first-party Management Console Command Line Interface (mccli) and the avtar/avmaint command set provide the scripted administrative surface alongside the API.

providers.name: Accrete
providers.description: Accrete is a dual-use enterprise and government AI company founded in 2017 and headquartered at 17 State Street, New York, that licenses specialized Expert AI Agents built on its Knowledge Engine Platform. The platform compresses tacit human domain expertise and unstructured data into autonomously constructed knowledge graphs, which its agents reason over with long-term memory and multi-agent collaboration. Its product lines are Argus for government — supply-chain FOCI risk, narrative intelligence, information operations and law enforcement — and Nebula for commercial customers, covering IT service management and change-risk prediction (Nebula ITSM, shipped as a Snowflake Native App) and social narrative and brand-influence detection (Nebula Social). Customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, U.S. Special Operations Command, the U.S. Army, and Fortune 500 companies in media and entertainment, consumer goods and gaming. Accrete publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract; its agents are delivered as licensed products and through partner marketplaces such as Snowflake.

providers.name: LemonLime
providers.description: LemonLime is a San Francisco company (Y Combinator, Summer 2026) building what it calls the AI knowledge layer for business — infrastructure that structures a company's documents, processes, customer history, and institutional knowledge into a foundation frontier models (GPT, Claude, Gemini) can retrieve and reason against. The platform connects to existing business systems (CRMs, document stores, ticketing, communication, and finance tools) over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), builds a structured representation of how the business operates, then deploys role- and workflow-specific AI agents on top of it, routing routine work to small fast models and reserving frontier reasoning models for tasks that need them. It is deliberately model-agnostic so the foundation survives frontier model generations. LemonLime does not train on customer business data on any plan, offers optional zero-data-retention, and markets compliance-aligned deployments for regulated industries. It sells a packaged SaaS product to non-technical teams and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation as of this profile.

providers.name: Rallyware
providers.description: Rallyware is an AI-powered sales performance and workforce enablement platform that guides distributed sellers, distributors, and field teams toward the next best action using real-time performance data, adaptive learning, gamification, and behavioral insights. It replaces fragmented enablement tools with a single orchestration system for large field and direct-selling organizations, and markets open APIs and pre-built connectors for CRM, POS, WFM, inventory, and HR systems. Rallyware runs a production REST API — JSON-LD/Hydra over API Platform, secured with OAuth2 — but does not publish it. There is no developer portal, no API reference and no OpenAPI, and the API is deployed one tenant per host and provisioned under an enterprise contract. The only public, machine-readable description of that API is Rallyware's own React Native SDK on npm, which ships the API client, its OAuth2 auth strategies, and an embeddable component library; the artifacts in this repository are derived from it.

providers.name: Chrome River (Emburse)
providers.description: Chrome River is an enterprise travel and expense (T&E) management platform now part of Emburse, offering expense reporting, invoice management, corporate card reconciliation, and travel spend controls for large and global organizations. The chromeriver.com brand now redirects to Emburse Enterprise; expense, invoice, and analytics data are exchanged through Emburse's gated API host (api.emburse.com) and app.chromeriver.com sign-in. Emburse publishes a broad compliance posture (SOC 1/2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001/27701/42001, PCI DSS, GDPR/CCPA/CPRA, TX-RAMP) via its trust center and operates a public responsible-disclosure program and Atlassian-hosted status page. This profile was surfaced as a Bain Capital Ventures portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Emburse's public surface; no open developer portal or OpenAPI is published, so spec-bearing artifacts are intentionally absent.

providers.name: BlackLine
providers.description: BlackLine is a cloud-based financial operations (FinOps) and accounting automation platform that helps finance and accounting teams automate the financial close, account reconciliation, journal entry, transaction matching, intercompany, consolidation integrity, and reporting processes. BlackLine exposes a suite of RESTful APIs on its developer portal so customers and partners can integrate the platform with ERP systems, banking platforms, payroll, and reporting tools — covering period management, user and team management, account reconciliation, journals, task management, transaction matching, and reporting. APIs authenticate with OAuth 2.0 client credentials. BlackLine (NASDAQ: BL) is a public company surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of ICONIQ Capital.

providers.name: Klarity
providers.description: Klarity is an enterprise AI company behind Klarity Architect, the "Enterprise Instinct Platform" — a Context Graph that captures how work actually happens inside a large organization and turns it into a living operational digital twin. The platform runs in three phases: Discover (an AI Companion that observes work, an AI Interviewer, and bulk file upload capture documented and undocumented processes), Structure (AI mapping organizes what it finds into a multi-level, role-aware Process Index from value streams down to individual activities), and Improve (an Advisor agent surfaces ROI-ranked recommendations and Signals detect drift from an approved standard). Klarity is used for finance, IT, GTM, HR and operations transformation, audit and compliance documentation, automation assessment, and SOP/PDD generation, with customers including DoorDash, Stripe, Salesforce and Uber. The product is delivered as a SaaS workspace with SAML SSO and fine-grained access control; Klarity publishes user documentation and an llms.txt index but no public developer API, SDKs, or webhook surface at the time of this profile.

providers.name: Riverbed Technology
providers.description: Riverbed Technology is an enterprise unified observability and digital-experience-management (DEM) company. Its platform spans network, application, infrastructure, cloud, and end-user experience monitoring. Core products include the Aternity DEM suite (employee, mobile, and customer experience), AppResponse / NetProfiler / NetIM network observability, SteelHead WAN optimization and the Data Express high-speed data movement service, and the Riverbed IQ AIOps intelligence layer for autonomous IT operations. Riverbed exposes secure APIs and a 50+ partner integrations library (ServiceNow, Splunk, PagerDuty, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and more) so teams can build and customize their own observability, ITSM, and automation workflows. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead, this profile has been enriched from Riverbed's public trust, security, and developer surfaces.

providers.name: CA Technologies (Broadcom)
providers.description: CA Technologies (originally Computer Associates) was a major enterprise software vendor focused on infrastructure management, DevOps, security, and mainframe software. It was acquired by Broadcom in November 2018 and its products are now part of Broadcom's Enterprise Software Division, including Layer 7 API Management, AppDynamics (later spun out to Cisco), DX Application Performance Management, Rally / Agile Central, Clarity PPM, BlazeMeter, AutoSys workload automation, and mainframe management suites. The primary developer portal is developer.broadcom.com.

providers.name: Intellectible
providers.description: Intellectible is an AI build platform for enterprise service providers - federal and state government contractors (GovCon), professional services firms, and economic development organizations - that turns portals, emails, CRM data, and market signals into structured opportunity, proposal, pricing, and knowledge workflows. Its horizontal build environment (project workspaces, visual workflows, document libraries, PostgreSQL databases, applications, pages, jobs, and queues) is exposed programmatically through the Intellectible Public API and a Code Execution SDK, letting teams run workflows synchronously, manage Library files, and query project databases directly from code.

providers.name: Levelpath
providers.description: Levelpath is an AI-native procurement platform that unifies intake and orchestration, strategic sourcing, contract lifecycle management, supplier management, third-party risk management, invoice automation, and category pipeline reporting into a single enterprise system. The product is built around AI agents that run sourcing events and generate RFPs, scan contract repositories to answer questions and flag risk, monitor supplier compliance signals, and process invoices. Levelpath is a closed enterprise platform: it operates customer and supplier applications at app.levelpath.com and supplierhub.levelpath.com, and its status page confirms a production APIs component, but it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. Integrations with SAP, Ariba, Coupa, Oracle, NetSuite, Docusign, Ironclad, OneTrust, Slack, and Microsoft Teams are delivered through the platform rather than a documented public API. Backed by Battery Ventures, Menlo Ventures, and Redpoint Ventures.

providers.name: Conexiom
providers.description: Conexiom is an AI-powered sales order and invoice automation platform for manufacturers and distributors. It captures order and document data from any format (PDFs, Excel, email bodies, scans, and handwritten notes), validates and corrects it against ERP systems, and pushes clean, touchless transactions into a customer's order-management workflow. The platform surfaces its own document API (retrieving document lists and attachments) and a set of ERP integrations, documented in an authenticated help center rather than a public developer portal. Conexiom is backed by ICONIQ Capital and runs on Microsoft Azure with a SOC 2 Type II and GDPR-aligned security posture.

providers.name: Archlet
providers.description: Archlet is an AI-native eSourcing, sourcing-optimization and eAuction platform, founded in 2018 in Zurich, Switzerland, that helps procurement teams run RFIs, RFPs, RFQs and reverse auctions faster and with more transparency. Its Spark AI engine automates RFx setup, auction configuration, scenario generation and bid summarization, while advanced bid analytics and scenario optimization unlock savings across strategic, tactical and tail-spend sourcing. Archlet exposes open, well-documented APIs for intake, CLM, reporting, supplier management and data-lake integrations that sync bi-directionally with ERP and P2P systems such as SAP, SAP Ariba, Coupa and Oracle. Trusted by enterprises including PepsiCo, TotalEnergies, Bosch, Walmart and FedEx, and backed by HV Capital.

providers.name: Scaled Cognition
providers.description: Scaled Cognition is a Mountain View, California AI model lab and enterprise platform company behind APT-1, the Agentic Pretrained Transformer — a frontier model the company says is pretrained on action prediction rather than token prediction and purpose-built for enterprise customer-experience agents. The commercial surface is an Agent Builder platform (Studio, a Python APT SDK, AgentTwin transcript-to-agent conversion, GenAPI simulation, Agent Evaluator, Agent Monitor and Agent Defender) exposed to customers through a stateless RESTful API that can run in Scaled Cognition's SOC 2 Type II cloud, in a customer VPC, or on-premises. Founded by Dan Roth (CEO), Dan Klein (CTO, UC Berkeley) and Damon Pender (CFO), the team previously built Semantic Machines, acquired by Microsoft in 2018. Backed by Khosla Ventures with a Genesys partnership. No public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable contract is published — the platform API and its OpenAPI live behind the Studio login.

providers.name: Fieldpoint
providers.description: Fieldpoint is an enterprise field service management (FSM) platform built for commercial contractors and service organizations across HVAC, electrical, fire inspection, security, medical equipment, and technology verticals. The platform covers the full service lifecycle including quoting, work order management, scheduling and dispatching, mobile technician apps, inventory tracking, service contracts, project costing, and customer management. Fieldpoint exposes an open REST API known as the Fieldpoint Data Transfer Service (FPDTS) that enables custom integrations with ERP, CRM, accounting, payroll, and workforce management systems. The platform ships pre-built connectors for Microsoft Dynamics GP/365, NetSuite, QuickBooks, Salesforce, WorkMarket, AvaTax, and more, while the FPDTS API allows enterprises to build bespoke integrations with any additional back-office system.

providers.name: Tresata
providers.description: Tresata is a Charlotte, North Carolina enterprise software company building what it describes as the foundational data layer for agentic AI. Its platform is marketed under the product names AB (Asset Builder), AU (Unreal Data Engine) and AF (Agent Foundation), alongside the Deduce and Discover surfaces, and automates data accuracy, entity resolution and enrichment across AWS, Azure and Google Cloud with a low-code interface. Pricing is usage-based, metered in Tresata Transaction Units (TTUs). Tresata publishes first-party open-source Scala/Spark libraries under the com.tresata group on Maven Central and co-authors the NANDini research effort with MIT on decentralised agentic data architectures. As of this profile it operates no public developer program: the platform is reached only through a login-gated tenant application, and no API reference, OpenAPI, GraphQL SDL, AsyncAPI or other machine-readable contract is published on any Tresata host.

providers.name: Artian
providers.description: Artian AI builds enterprise-grade agentic AI systems for financial services, letting banks, brokerages, insurers and other regulated institutions turn complex, business-critical workflows into autonomous multi-agent operations with humans fully in control. The platform pairs an AI Agent Builder and autonomous planner with domain-specific Workflow Agents, and ships governance as a first-class feature - end-to-end data lineage, model risk management, immutable audit logs, in-band policy guardrails and circuit breakers - so agents can operate safely inside strict regulatory and data-residency boundaries. Artian deploys on-prem or into a customer VPC on Kubernetes rather than as a public multi-tenant service, and interoperates via REST, MCP and A2A. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in New York, it is backed by Anthemis, Foxe Capital, Work-Bench and Wormhole Capital.

providers.name: Zend
providers.description: Zend is the enterprise PHP platform business of Perforce Software, providing production-grade PHP runtimes, tooling, and long-term support for mission-critical applications. Its portfolio spans ZendPHP (a hardened, enterprise-supported PHP runtime with LTS builds for end-of-life PHP versions), ZendHQ (PHP application observability and monitoring), Zend Server, Zend Studio, and Zend Guard, along with migration, modernization, performance auditing, and Black Belt support services for Laravel, Symfony, CodeIgniter, and CakePHP teams. Zend ships product tooling and a documentation surface rather than a public REST API.

providers.name: Summation
providers.description: Summation is an enterprise AI analyst platform that automates recurring business work — financial reviews, forecasts, models, and executive-ready decks — by connecting to a company's data sources (ERPs, data warehouses, and spreadsheets) and producing verified, source-traced reports in the format teams already use. Its AI agent "Addison" runs playbooks across finance, operations, and sales, tracing every number back to its source so outputs are audit-ready and SOC 2 Type II compliant. Founded by Ian Wong (CEO) and Ramachandran "RC" Ramarathinam (CTO), formerly of Opendoor, Summation is backed by Battery Ventures. The company operates a customer application, product documentation, and a public Trust Center, but does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Cerenovus
providers.description: Cerenovus Inc. (cerenovus.ai) is a San Francisco AI software company backed by Y Combinator (S26 batch). Cerenovus is both the company and the product — earlier product names have been retired, and Compendium is its internal workspace rather than a public offering. It reads the records an organization already produces (email, contracts, invoices, ledgers, tickets, calendars, meeting notes and documents), resolves the same customer, vendor or person across systems into one entity, runs deterministic scans for countable problems such as duplicate payments, dormant vendors and missed discount windows, then uses models to investigate what the scans surface and returns ranked findings with every claim cited back to the source record. It is sold as eight standalone engagements — operational due diligence, value creation plan, post-merger integration, exit readiness, operational diagnostic, decision intelligence, operational foresight and early warning, and spend and vendor intelligence — to enterprises, middle-market companies, private equity firms, consulting and advisory firms, and corporate development teams. Cerenovus publishes no developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification; the only machine surface found is an undocumented, OAuth-protected remote MCP server at api.cerenovus.ai/mcp. Not affiliated with the similarly named Johnson & Johnson MedTech neurovascular device business.

providers.name: ST Labs
providers.description: ST Labs (Standard Template Labs, stlabs.com) is an AI-native IT service management platform that turns historical ticket data, knowledge bases, and enterprise integrations into instant resolutions, automated workflows, and a living graph of the organization. Its capabilities span smart ticket enrichment (auto-classify, prioritize, attach resolution context), AI clustering into self-healing workflows, AI-agent self-service, and a "Digital Twin" / Axiom context graph that maps real-time relationships between people, applications, infrastructure, and processes and is queryable in natural language. The product connects to 100+ systems (ServiceNow, Okta, AWS, Datadog, Slack, Workday, and more) across ITSM, identity, cloud, security, and collaboration. As of mid-2026 the company is in early-access/waitlist stage with no public developer API, and is backed by CRV and ICONIQ Capital.

providers.name: Trope
providers.description: Trope is an AI-native platform that helps ERP implementation partners deliver successful implementations faster, deploying AI agents across discovery, requirements, fit-gap analysis, data migration, approval workflows, UAT scripts, training guides, documentation, and go-live readiness — built for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central consultancies and other implementation teams. Trope also maintains Trope CUA, an open-source MCP-native computer-use agent for background desktop automation on Windows and macOS. Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, based in San Francisco.

providers.name: Prysm
providers.description: Prysm — legally Motherson Prysm, Inc. — builds large-format interactive display hardware and the Prysm Application Suite, a cloud-hosted visual collaboration and digital-workplace platform. Founded in 2005 in Silicon Valley as Spudnik by Amit Jain and Roger Hajjar, the company invented and patented Laser Phosphor Display (LPD) technology, shipped today as the bezel-free LPD 6K Series single-panel display (up to 225 inches) alongside an 85-inch LCD room solution. In 2014 Prysm merged with Anacore to add a multi-source interactive canvas, producing a platform that combines digital whiteboarding, on-screen annotation, co-browsing, device sharing and Teams/Zoom/Webex launching across web, desktop and iPhone clients for customer experience centers, executive boardrooms and huddle rooms. Prysm became part of the Motherson Group in 2025. Prysm announced an early preview of a "Prysm API" for custom applications on its digital workplace platform in June 2017, but publishes no developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification today.

providers.name: Enzai
providers.description: Enzai is an enterprise AI governance platform that helps organizations adopt AI while managing regulatory and operational risk. Its product suite spans agentic AI governance (real-time analysis, risk flagging, and agent-sprawl management), AI use-case intake and approval workflows, a centralized AI registry inventorying first- and third-party AI systems, and compliance frameworks that map AI initiatives to the EU AI Act, GDPR, NIST AI RMF, and ISO/IEC 42001. Enzai is headquartered in Belfast with a London office, is ISO 27001 certified, and is backed by venture capital including Seedcamp. No public API or developer portal is published at this time.

providers.name: Calypso
providers.description: APIs and developer resources for Nasdaq Calypso (formerly Adenza / Calypso Technology), a cross-asset front-to-back capital markets technology platform for trading, risk management, collateral, treasury, processing, and accounting used by banks, asset managers, central banks, and clearing houses worldwide.

providers.name: BetterUp
providers.description: BetterUp is an enterprise Human Transformation Platform that combines human and AI-powered coaching, grounded in behavioral science and enterprise data, to help organizations develop leaders, managers, and their broader workforce. Founded by Alexi Robichaux, BetterUp serves 750+ enterprise customers including Google, Salesforce, Moderna, and Workday, with a network of 4,000+ coaches across 70+ countries. The platform delivers leadership development, manager effectiveness, AI coaching, and workforce resilience programs. BetterUp is HR-tech / organizational-development software and exposes no public developer API; platform integration is delivered through packaged enterprise connectors (Workday, Salesforce, Slack, Microsoft Viva, SAP SuccessFactors, Degreed) plus HRIS and SSO provisioning. Sector: hr-tech.

providers.name: CACI International
providers.description: CACI International provides information technology, professional services, and managed solutions to U.S. federal government agencies in the defense, intelligence, homeland security, and civilian markets. The company delivers expertise and technology across C3I, cyber, digital solutions, enterprise IT, mission support, space, and spectrum superiority domains.

providers.name: Orolabs
providers.description: ORO Labs provides an agentic procurement orchestration platform for enterprise spend management. It coordinates people, processes, systems, and data so employees can get what they need without friction, unifying intake management, supplier onboarding and lifecycle, risk and compliance orchestration, and AI-driven workflow automation. The platform offers a no-code workflow builder, a purpose-built agent builder for custom procurement AI agents, and bring-your-own-LLM flexibility, with secure, semantically rich integrations across the procuretech landscape. ORO Labs is backed by Felicis and Norwest Venture Partners.

providers.name: CO2 AI
providers.description: CO2 AI is an enterprise sustainability platform that helps organizations measure, reduce, and report carbon emissions across their entire value chain. It combines trustworthy emissions data, AI-powered workflows, and supply-chain collaboration to baseline and track Scope 1, 2, and 3 corporate footprints, compute audit-ready product carbon footprints (PCF) at scale across thousands of SKUs (PACT, TfS, PEF, ISO aligned), engage suppliers for primary data, and build decarbonization plans ranked by Marginal Abatement Cost. Backed by Partech and surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a climate-sector company profile. No public developer API is published as of this enrichment pass; the profile captures the company's security, trust, and legal surface.

providers.name: Leah
providers.description: Leah, formerly ContractPodAi and legally ContractPod Technologies Limited, is a London-headquartered enterprise agentic AI company that unifies contract lifecycle management, legal transformation, procurement, and finance operations into a single autonomous system. Its Leah Agentic OS platform provides skills-based orchestration, agentic workflows, a natural-language app builder, a library of domain-specific legal, contracting, procurement, and finance agents, and the Leah Maestro enterprise orchestrator. Leah is a five-time Gartner CLM Visionary, is SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified, and is used by enterprises including PwC, KPMG, Philips, Alaska Airlines, MUFG, and Cushman & Wakefield. Leah ships pre-built connectors and describes open REST APIs for enterprise integration, but maintains no public developer portal or published API reference — API access is unlocked through the enterprise contract.

providers.name: Toonimo
providers.description: Toonimo is a digital adoption platform (DAP) that overlays personalized, interactive on-screen guidance onto enterprise software and websites. Using patented voice, text-bubble, and visual-cue walkthroughs, Toonimo guides end users and employees through onboarding, self-service, and complex workflows to increase conversions, accelerate software adoption, and reduce support costs. It layers on top of platforms such as Salesforce, SAP SuccessFactors, Workday, ServiceNow, Oracle Cloud, Microsoft Dynamics, Coupa, and SharePoint, and enables subject-matter experts (not just developers) to build and maintain adoption content. Toonimo is a marketing/product company backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners; it does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Zinier
providers.description: Zinier is a no-code field service management platform that helps enterprises schedule and manage their workforce, assets, and customers, powered by generative AI. Its office and field experiences pair ready-to-use productivity tools with a no-code Task Builder for building custom workflows, and an Integration Marketplace advertising 1,000+ out-of-the-box connections to ERP, CRM, and EAM systems such as SAP, Oracle, Microsoft, Salesforce, Zendesk, ServiceNow, IBM, and Infor. Zinier targets asset-intensive field-service operations, from scheduling and dispatch through mobile task execution and customer communication. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and ICONIQ Capital. No public developer API, API reference, or OpenAPI surface is published today — integration is delivered through the marketplace and end-user product documentation.

providers.name: Sycamore
providers.description: Sycamore (Sycamore Labs, Inc.) is a Palo Alto, California company building a "trusted agent operating system for the enterprise" — a platform for large organizations to build, deploy, and orchestrate autonomous AI agents across their existing systems with enterprise-grade security, human oversight, and organizational intelligence that compounds over time. Its stated pillars are a progressive trust system where agents earn autonomy through demonstrated reliability, adaptive system generation from natural language, continuous learning from outcomes, and collective multi-agent coordination. The company emerged from stealth in March 2026 with a $65M seed round led by Coatue and Lightspeed. As of this profile Sycamore is pre-product with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this repo captures its public company identity, security posture, and machine-readable llms.txt.

providers.name: DigiLens
providers.description: DigiLens Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California company that designs and manufactures holographic waveguide optics and augmented reality display systems for extended reality (XR). Its Crystal Waveguides are produced with a proprietary photopolymer material set, inkjet printing and a holographic contact-copy process rather than etching, and are supplied to partners including Samsung, Corning, Panasonic, Sony, Continental, Mitsubishi Chemical and Goertek for smartglasses, automotive head-up displays, smart helmets and avionics head-up guidance. DigiLens also ships ARGO, a standalone, rugged enterprise AR headset running DigiOS — an Android-based operating system with voice UI, gaze and scroll-wheel interaction, projector control and Microsoft Intune MDM certification. Developers build for ARGO in Unity or Android Studio on top of the DigiOS SDK and Qualcomm Snapdragon Spaces, with samples published in the digilens-ar GitHub organization and documentation on the DigiLens developer portal. DigiLens has raised a Series D led by Samsung Electronics at a valuation above $500M.

providers.name: Thorin
providers.description: Thorin is an applied-AI startup incubated and backed by 8VC (Joe Lonsdale), building a workbench for company agents. Its product at app.thorin.com pairs a personal agent that acts as your delegate with project agents that own shared team workflows, connecting business systems (Slack, Google Workspace, Notion, Gong, Salesforce, Affinity, and MCP) and organizing company context into feeds that power reusable skills and scheduled automations. Thorin observes work across email, chat, meetings, and documents to build a real-time model of how a business operates, then automates recurring processes such as deal flow, deal-prep briefs, and inbox switchboards. Seed-stage, based in San Francisco. This profile documents Thorin's product and documentation surface; no public developer API is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Hanover Park
providers.description: Hanover Park is an AI-native ERP and fund administration platform for private market investors, unifying fund accounting, portfolio intelligence, and the LP experience in a single system of record. It pairs a proprietary general ledger, waterfall engine, investor portal, and portfolio management layer with AI agents that read email, propose journal entries, and extract portfolio updates, all reviewed by expert fund accountants. The platform automates capital calls, cash reconciliation, general-ledger posting, KPI collection, and reporting for venture capital, private equity, and other private-market firms. Founded in 2024 and headquartered around a modern back-office thesis, Hanover Park raised a $27M Series A led by Emergence Capital (with Lux Capital and Susa Ventures) and has grown from $1B to $15B in assets under administration. The company is SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II certified with a zero-trust, client-isolated AI architecture. No public API or developer program is published at this time; the product is delivered as a login-gated SaaS application.

providers.name: JMS
providers.description: Java Message Service (JMS), now known as Jakarta Messaging, is a Java API that allows applications to create, send, receive, and read messages. It defines a common enterprise messaging API for loosely coupled, reliable, and asynchronous communication between distributed application components. Current release is Jakarta Messaging 3.1 (Jakarta EE 10).

providers.name: WorkForce Software
providers.description: WorkForce Software, an ADP company since October 2024, makes the WorkForce Suite, an enterprise workforce management platform covering time and attendance, employee scheduling, absence and leave management, labor forecasting, data capture, and payroll compliance for large, complex organizations. The Suite integrates with leading HCM and ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, Workday, ADP) via RESTful APIs, SOAP APIs, and file-based interfaces, with SSO/SLO and MFA support; API and integration documentation is provided to customers through the WorkForce Software community portal rather than a public developer portal.

providers.name: Roper Technologies
providers.description: Roper Technologies is a diversified technology holding company (NASDAQ: ROP) that acquires, manages, and develops niche market-leading software and technology-enabled businesses. Over three-quarters of revenue comes from software products across three segments: Application Software (legal, healthcare, government, education, and insurance vertical SaaS), Network Software (construction, transportation, and insurance network platforms), and Technology Enabled Products (medical devices, industrial, and RF identification). Key subsidiaries include Aderant (legal software), Clinisys (laboratory informatics), Deltek (project-based business ERP), Frontline Education (K-12 HR software), Vertafore (insurance technology), IntelliTrans (supply chain visibility), ConstructConnect (construction information), DAT Solutions (freight matching), and iPipeline (life insurance SaaS).

providers.name: SAP America
providers.description: SAP America, Inc. is the US subsidiary of SAP SE, headquartered in Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, and serving as the Americas headquarters for the parent company's enterprise software portfolio (ERP, SCM, CRM, HCM, analytics, and cloud platform). SAP America itself does not publish a US-specific developer portal or APIs distinct from the parent SAP SE surface — all API documentation, SDKs, and OpenAPI artifacts are catalogued under the sibling `sap` repository (api.sap.com, SAP Business Accelerator Hub, SAP BTP). This repo is a subsidiary placeholder that exists to (1) record SAP America as a distinct US legal entity for partnership, public-sector, procurement, and FedRAMP / GovCloud contexts, and (2) cross-link to related US-only sibling subsidiaries — most importantly SAP NS2 (SAP National Security Services), the independent US subsidiary that operates SAP workloads in the Cloud Intelligence Enterprise (CIE), the DoD cloud environment, and the Commercially Regulated Environment (CRE) for federal, defense, and intelligence community customers. No tier-1 API artifacts (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, JSON Schema, capabilities, plans, rate limits, FinOps) are generated in this repo per the api-evangelist no-empty-artifact rule — they are maintained under the parent `sap` repo and the per-product child repos (`sap-business-technology-platform`, `sap-successfactors`, `sap-ariba`, `sap-concur`, `sap-fieldglass`, `sap-api-management`, `sap-integration-suite`).

providers.name: Eudia
providers.description: Eudia is an enterprise augmented-intelligence platform for in-house legal, compliance, and procurement teams at large organizations and government agencies. Its "Enterprise Brain" ingests a company's contracts, policies, precedents, and prior decisions and codifies the judgment of its legal experts into governed AI workflows, while "Expert Digital Twins" let business teams self-serve governed legal guidance without direct attorney involvement. Products span compliance automation, contracting, decision self-service, mergers and acquisitions, and litigation support, with connectors into Microsoft, Google Drive, SharePoint, Box, Salesforce, DocuSign, OnIt, and LinkSquares. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, Eudia raised a Series A of up to $105M led by General Catalyst with Sierra Ventures, Floodgate, and Defy Partners. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity, trust, and security posture.

providers.name: ServiceMax
providers.description: ServiceMax is asset-centric field service management (FSM) software that helps equipment manufacturers and service organizations maximize equipment uptime, optimize technician productivity, and streamline service delivery. Its cloud platform, built natively on the Salesforce platform (ServiceMax Core and Asset 360), spans work order and workflow management, scheduling and dispatch (Service Board), preventive and predictive maintenance, contract and entitlement management, parts and inventory, offline-capable mobile tools (ServiceMax Go), real-time technician collaboration (Zinc), and customer self-service (Engage). Founded in 2007 and acquired by PTC in 2023, ServiceMax integrates with PTC's IoT and PLM portfolio (ThingWorx, Windchill) and exposes its data and workflows through the underlying Salesforce API surface rather than a standalone public developer API.

providers.name: Naboo
providers.description: Naboo is Reasoning Layer infrastructure for enterprise AI agents, built on a Decision Graph that models how a company actually decides, ships, and unblocks - who decided what, what triggered each decision, what blocks it, and what depends on it - across code, tickets, pull requests, docs, Slack, runtime, and internal services. Any AI agent in the organization queries the graph in GraphQL, or through an MCP server that turns plain intent into a structured query, and gets a structured answer instead of a list of search results. Naboo deploys on-premise or in a customer VPC with zero data egress, integrates with any LLM (OpenAI, Anthropic, Llama, Mistral) and agentic framework (LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI), and enforces existing role-based access controls at retrieval time. Founded in 2023 by Gilad Salinger (CEO) and Dror Wolmer (CTO), with production customers Global-E (NASDAQ: GLBE) and Melio.

providers.name: Aily Labs
providers.description: Aily Labs is a Munich-based enterprise AI company that builds an AI Decision Intelligence Suite — a platform that connects siloed internal and external data to deliver real-time, explainable predictions and recommendations across Finance, R&D, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Quality, Go-To-Market, Procurement, and People functions. The suite ships with 300+ validated predictive models and an iOS app, and is deployed across Healthcare & Life Sciences, Consumer Goods, Luxury & Fashion, Media & Tech, Retail, and Services (clients include Sanofi). Aily Labs is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. It exposes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's corporate, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: IgniteTech
providers.description: IgniteTech is a global, AI-first enterprise software company (headquartered in Austin, Texas, and operating remote-first across 30+ countries) that acquires, revitalizes, and supports mission-critical enterprise software and embeds AI-powered capabilities across its portfolio — an operating model the company brands "AI-DNA." Its Native AI products include Eloquens AI (automated, context-aware email response), MyPersonas (AI digital clones of key employees that answer repetitive questions via a video chat-style interface), and Adminio AI (meeting scheduling through intelligent email orchestration). The IgniteTech Unlimited software library spans acquired enterprise brands such as GFI Software, Khoros (Communities and Care), Jive, DNN, Gensym, Computron, GRID (supply chain, via the Suuchi acquisition), Knova, AnswerHub, ACORN, TradeBeam, and SalesBuilder. Led by CEO Eric Vaughan, the company positions itself as an AI enterprise software company rather than only a software holding company.

providers.name: Syndio
providers.description: Syndio is an enterprise workplace-equity and compensation-governance software company. Its AI-assisted platform helps large organizations make defensible, compliant pay decisions at scale, spanning offers, promotions, merit cycles, and pay-equity/pay-transparency compliance (including EU Pay Transparency Directive requirements). The platform is organized into Essentials (foundations for aligned, compliant pay decisions), Decisions (real-time guidance during pay decision-making), and Predict (forward-looking workforce intelligence), all powered by the domain-specific Syndi AI. Syndio reports governing more than $1T in pay decisions for 350+ global enterprises. It is delivered as a closed enterprise SaaS accessed via the app with OAuth 2 / SSO; there is no public self-serve developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI definition. First-party developer-facing surfaces are limited to the syndioctl command-line tool and a public GitHub organization. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: Apiphani
providers.description: Apiphani is a technology-enabled application managed-services company dedicated to helping businesses minimize the effort and risk of running their tier-1, mission-critical applications. It combines decades of enterprise operations experience with intelligent automation and machine learning to drive efficiency and reliability across SAP environments (S/4HANA, Business Suite, Cloud ERP) running on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Services span application technical management (ABAP, SAP Basis, application security), application hosting (ALM/APM), application infrastructure (auto-scaling, HA/DR), security management, and cloud migration and optimization. Apiphani's Luumen platform is an AI-native observability product with "Deep Automation" that detects and resolves issues before users notice, unifying application telemetry, security, and self-healing. The company is certified SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and CSA STAR, and is backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: CDW
providers.description: CDW is a leading multi-brand provider of information technology solutions to business, government, education, and healthcare customers. CDW offers eProcurement integration capabilities including a Catalog API, PunchOut (cXML/OCI), electronic purchase ordering, and electronic invoicing to enable procurement system integration with partners such as SAP Ariba, Coupa, Oracle, and Jaggaer.

providers.name: Scoutbee
providers.description: Scoutbee is an AI-powered supplier discovery and procurement intelligence platform that helps enterprise buyers instantly find, vet, and connect with trusted suppliers. Founded in 2015 in Berlin, Germany, Scoutbee uses large language models, knowledge-graph technology, and a global supplier network to power supplier discovery, sourcing project execution (Streamline), and a centralized supplier data foundation (DeepSee), surfaced through the Scoutbee Intelligence Platform. Its AI gives procurement, sourcing, and category-management teams recommendations for suppliers matched on qualifications, risk, certifications, sustainability, diversity, cost, and experience. Scoutbee integrates with SAP Ariba guided sourcing and, following its October 2025 acquisition by Coupa, is being embedded into the Coupa Supplier Portal. Scoutbee does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal; this profile captures its public identity and web surface.

providers.name: Section AI
providers.description: Section AI (formerly Section School) is an enterprise AI training and adoption platform that helps large organizations turn AI investment into measurable workforce transformation and ROI. Its two products are Section HQ, a command center for Heads of AI to track usage, measure "AI fitness," surface real-time insights, and manage transformation roadmaps; and Section Coach, personalized AI coaching that delivers skills training, certification programs, and workflow identification to employees and teams. Section also runs AI transformation planning, leadership coaching, AI strategy support, workflow automation, and agentic AI workshops for enterprises of 100+ employees, with customers including Johnson & Johnson, Nike, Okta, Unilever, Mercer, and Publicis. Backed by General Catalyst and led by founder Greg Shove. As of this profile the company exposes a web/app product surface (app.sectionai.com) but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation.

providers.name: Talk-A-Bot
providers.description: Talk-A-Bot is a Budapest-based, Techstars-backed enterprise chatbot company building compliance-first conversational AI for regulated industries including banking, healthcare, government, retail, and HR. Its platform emphasizes "zero hallucination" answers grounded only in verified knowledge bases, full conversation logging and audit trails, EU-based infrastructure with on-premise deployment options, and daily human review. Products include an FAQ Chatbot, an Agentic Chatbot, FeedbackHub, and the CHEQ internal-communications assistant, deployed across web, mobile, Messenger, and Viber. The company markets an API-first architecture for integrating with customer systems (CRM, ERP, payments, ticketing, HR) but publishes no public self-serve developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK; engagement is full-service. Compliance posture spans HIPAA, DORA, the EU AI Act, GDPR, and PCI DSS.

providers.name: Cadence Design Systems
providers.description: Cadence Design Systems is a multinational electronic design automation (EDA) software and hardware company. Cadence provides tools for designing integrated circuits, systems on chips, printed circuit boards, and pharmaceutical drugs, with a portfolio that includes Virtuoso, Spectre, Genus, Innovus, JasperGold, Xcelium, Palladium, Allegro, OrCAD, and AI tools such as Cerebrus and ChipGPT.

providers.name: Tamr
providers.description: An enterprise data management company that uses machine learning to automate the mastering, enrichment, and classification of messy data across disparate sources. Helps large organizations unify customer, supplier, and product data to power analytics and AI initiatives.

providers.name: Sunyur
providers.description: Sunyur (商越科技 / Beijing Sunyur Network Technology Co., Ltd, 北京商越网络科技有限公司) is a Chinese enterprise procurement digitalization company providing AI-driven procurement solutions for large and medium enterprises. Its products include an intelligent procurement middle-platform (采购中台), an SRM supplier relationship management system, an e-procurement SaaS platform, and a procurement mall (采购商城), helping each customer build a dedicated online, digital, and intelligent enterprise procurement platform to raise efficiency and lower cost. Sunyur operates an open integration platform ("聚贤阁", open.sunyur.com) that connects enterprises to 30+ mainstream e-commerce platforms and 10+ third-party applications through a single accessToken-authenticated API surface. Sunyur is backed by Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Axiamatic
providers.description: Axiamatic is an enterprise-transformation AI platform that aims to de-risk and accelerate large modernization programs, claiming to cut up to 50% off the cost and timeline of enterprise transformations. Its agentic platform combines a Living Context Graph (a digital twin of a transformation program built from structured and unstructured data), autonomous Transformation Agents that detect risks such as translation loss, resistance, and cross-stream drift, role-specific Playbooks delivered into existing workflows, and Axia, an AI assistant available via voice, chat, Microsoft Teams, or Slack. It targets ERP modernization (SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics 365), CRM consolidation (Salesforce, Dynamics), and supply-chain and business transformation. The company is backed by Greylock and announced a $54M raise. It was surfaced as a Greylock portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it currently publishes a marketing site and a login application (app.axiamatic.com) but no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Kyrok
providers.description: Kyrok GmbH is a Berlin-based software company building an AI operating system for mid-sized pharmaceutical and chemical manufacturers in Europe. The platform layers over a company's existing ERP (SAP S/4HANA, SAP R/3, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Infor, Applus) and connects the systems supply chain teams currently hold together by hand into intelligent operations across customer service, production planning, material planning and procurement. Kyrok positions itself on an "AI assists, people decide" model, running on European infrastructure in Frankfurt am Main, GDPR-compliant, with ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 certifications in progress. The company announced a EUR 3.1M round in June 2026 and names AnalytiChem and Konapharma as customers. Kyrok connects to ERP systems via API but publishes no public developer API, API reference, or SDKs as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Conduct AI
providers.description: Conduct AI (conduct.ai) is an enterprise "AI operating system" that helps IT teams understand, operate, and transform their business software, starting with SAP and expanding across the wider enterprise stack. Its platform analyzes custom code to reveal dependencies and system relationships (Understand), automates software-development workflows from planning through deployment (Operate), and accelerates system migrations such as S/4HANA with automated analysis and code refactoring (Transform). The company markets outcomes like faster S/4HANA migration planning, reduced manual system analysis, and shorter change-implementation cycles. Conduct raised a $60M Series A and is backed by ICONIQ Capital. It publishes a marketing site, blog, and case studies but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or API reference documentation.

providers.name: LightSource
providers.description: LightSource is an AI-native direct materials procurement platform that connects engineering, procurement, and suppliers across the full sourcing lifecycle from concept to award. The product automates RFX creation and distribution, AI-assisted bid analysis, supplier collaboration and quote normalization across custom quote formats, and ongoing cost tracking, with more than 20,000 suppliers live on the network. It is sold to procurement and supply-chain teams in automotive, electronics, chemicals, medical devices, construction, and forest products, and the company reports sourcing cost reductions of 3-25% for customers including Time Manufacturing (Versalift), Arxada, BRP, and Canada Goose. LightSource is SOC 2 Type 2 attested and supports SSO and role-based access control. As of July 2026 the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification; its docs host is an end-user and supplier help center.

providers.name: Topia
providers.description: Topia is a global mobility platform for distributed workforces, used by HR, Finance and Legal teams at mid-market and enterprise companies to manage international assignments, relocations, business travel, remote work and cross-border compliance across 190+ countries in a single system. Founded in 2010 and headquartered in the United States, with additional offices in the United Kingdom, Ireland and Estonia, Topia spans global talent mobility, a tax and compliance engine, cost estimation and tracking, global workforce planning, cost and immigration risk management, and business travel. In April 2026 Topia launched Horizon, an agentic AI workspace for mobility teams that the company describes as built natively into MCP (Model Context Protocol) environments. Topia integrates with HRIS, payroll, travel and expense systems including Workday (a Workday Approved Integration), SAP, ADP, Oracle, Ceridian, SAP Concur and BCD Travel. Topia publishes an llms.txt at its marketing host, but no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification; the support center sits behind a customer login.

providers.name: IrisVR
providers.description: IrisVR is a virtual-reality software company for the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry, best known for its two products: Prospect, a desktop application that converts Revit, SketchUp, Rhino, Navisworks and other 3D/BIM models into immersive VR walkthroughs in one click, and Scope, a mobile app for viewing and sharing 360-degree panoramas on standalone and phone-based VR headsets. Founded in New York, IrisVR was acquired by The Wild in 2021, and The Wild (together with IrisVR) was subsequently acquired by Autodesk in 2022. The products and support site remain available. IrisVR does not publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity, packages, and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Collibra
providers.description: Collibra is a data intelligence company providing a cloud-based platform for data governance, cataloging, quality, lineage, and AI governance. The Collibra Data Intelligence Platform helps enterprises discover, understand, govern, and trust their data assets through automated lineage tracking, policy management, data observability, and collaborative stewardship. The Collibra developer ecosystem includes REST APIs, GraphQL Knowledge Graph API, workflow automation, and a broad library of source connectors.

providers.name: Appify
providers.description: Appify is an enterprise application platform that lets organizations build, extend, and migrate line-of-business software without traditional development. The company markets a model-driven, AI-native platform — apps are described in natural language and the platform generates the data model, UI, permissions, workflows, and analytics — plus an "Unshackle" AI agent that extends systems of record such as Salesforce, SAP, and Oracle, or replicates an existing SaaS application on Appify-owned infrastructure. Appify states 40+ enterprise integrations, 12+ industries in production, and 20M+ transactions processed, and its published pricing includes "REST API access" and "unlimited apps, objects, endpoints" as standard capabilities. No public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification is published; the API surface sits behind the tenant login.

providers.name: Zscaler
providers.description: Zscaler is a cloud security platform delivering Zero Trust Exchange services including Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA), Zscaler Private Access (ZPA), and Zscaler Digital Experience (ZDX). Zscaler exposes REST APIs across its product suite for configuration, policy management, and reporting, authenticated via API keys, OAuth 2.0, or session-based authentication depending on the product and cloud (zsapi).

providers.name: BlackSwan Technologies
providers.description: BlackSwan Technologies is an enterprise AI software company founded in 2014 by Michael and Elinoar Ouliel, headquartered in London with engineering across Israel, Poland and India. Its flagship product, ELEMENT, is marketed as an Enterprise AI Operating System: a low/no-code platform-as-a-service combining a data fabric, knowledge graphs, machine learning and composite AI so banks and other regulated enterprises can assemble applications for KYC on demand, enhanced due diligence, financial crime, transaction intelligence, market intelligence and underwriting without first consolidating their data. Its software engineering unit, BST LABS, built and open-sourced CAIOS (Cloud AI Operating System) and a family of Python developer tools (DynaCLI, CLVM, PyJdict, PyComposite, AuthK). BlackSwan Technologies was acquired by HUB Cyber Security Ltd. (NASDAQ: HUBC) in a stock-for-stock transaction that closed on 27 January 2025, and its corporate domain blackswantechnologies.ai no longer resolves in DNS; the secured data fabric technology is now marketed under HUB Technologies. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract (OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, MCP, A2A) was found for BlackSwan Technologies during enrichment.

providers.name: Mechanical Orchard
providers.description: Mechanical Orchard is an enterprise software company, founded by Pivotal veterans, that modernizes mission-critical legacy and mainframe systems. Its flagship platform, Imogen, uses AI to observe how legacy applications actually behave, then incrementally rewrites them into modern, cloud-ready code while continuously verifying that behavior is preserved so nothing breaks during migration. The company pairs the Imogen platform with professional services and a free proof of concept, integrates with AWS Transform and Google Cloud, and serves both commercial enterprises and government agencies looking to retire risky COBOL and mainframe estates. It is backed by Bloomberg Beta, Emergence Capital, and GV.

providers.name: Zmanda
providers.description: Zmanda is an enterprise backup and recovery software provider and the commercial steward of the open-source Amanda (Advanced Maryland Automatic Network Disk Archiver) project. Its products protect Linux, Windows and macOS systems, databases, and application data with agent-based and agentless backups that write to local disk, tape, and public-cloud object storage. The company maintains an active GitHub organization (github.com/zmanda) around the Amanda backup engine and related tooling, operates a customer-facing management portal at the Zmanda Network (network.zmanda.com), and publishes API documentation for programmatic backup and recovery management at api.zmanda.com. Zmanda was an early portfolio company of Canaan Partners.

providers.name: Assemble
providers.description: Assemble builds autonomous AI agents that help enterprise IT and business-systems teams automate development work inside core platforms such as Salesforce, SAP, Workday, and NetSuite. The agents scope changes across integrated ERP, CRM, and HRIS systems, understand cross-system dependencies, implement and validate modifications, and keep a complete audit trail so teams can review agent work, approve modifications, and revert individual changes or restore a system to a prior state. Assemble is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) company targeting IT and business-systems teams managing complex enterprise transformations. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or OpenAPI, so only its verified public identity and website properties are captured.

providers.name: Draxon
providers.description: Draxon is a Berlin-based company (founded 2025, backed by HV Capital and Point Nine) that provides IATA-certified virtual reality training for airport ground handling operations. The platform ships pre-configured Meta Quest VR headsets and an immersive training library covering ramp equipment such as belt loaders, tractors, pushback tugs, GPUs and towable stairs, plus safety procedures and hand signals for frontline ramp personnel. Its Trainer Hub delivers automated, IATA-compliant certification tracking with self-paced or instructor-led modules. Draxon operates as a B2B SaaS training provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: AiSensum
providers.description: AiSensum (AISensum) builds agentic AI "teammates" that work alongside front-line staff to drive revenue, improve quality, and reduce labour while keeping the human in the lead. Operating since 2017 with a presence across Southeast Asia, it deploys purpose-built AI teammates for enterprise front-line operations in retail, F&B, hospitality and entertainment, each specialising in one measurable outcome: Daniel (revenue teammate, personalised counter offers/upsell), Sasha (time and cost teammate, bulk product-photo editing and approval), and Nicole (progress teammate, conversation scoring and cashier coaching against brand SOPs). Deployments are scoped through a half-day IFA (Intelligent Front-line Automation) Workshop. AiSensum publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal; it is a portfolio company of 500 Global tracked in the API Evangelist network. This profile was enriched from the company's public web presence and an on-site llms.txt.

providers.name: Banyansoftware
providers.description: Banyan Software is a global acquirer and permanent operator of vertical market software (VMS) businesses, headquartered in Toronto, Canada. Built as an "evergreen" alternative to private equity, Banyan buys profitable, growing enterprise software companies that hold dominant positions in niche markets (typically $2M-$30M in annual revenue) and holds them for the long term rather than reselling. It has acquired 100+ companies across sectors including healthcare IT, education, manufacturing, broadcast, public sector, and fintech, and supports them through a Growth Ops team spanning AI, talent, sales and marketing, payments, product, finance, cybersecurity, and legal. Banyan Software is a holding/operating company and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: HumanQ
providers.description: HumanQ is an execution-capability and intelligence platform that helps organizations move critical work forward through structured, live execution sprints called QPods. Each QPod is a 60-minute facilitated session, led by trained "Catalysts," for small groups of up to six participants working through decision drag, unclear ownership, and cross-team stalls. HumanQ is offered as HumanQ Scale (an enterprise-wide program with weekly and monthly tracks, on-demand drop-ins, and deep customization) and HumanQ Teams (a manager-led tool for up to four groups, live in two weeks with no contract). Progress is tracked through the QStart, QImpact, and QSignal measurement framework, with delivery across 74 countries. HumanQ is a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures. It is a managed-services platform and does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Workhelix
providers.description: Workhelix is an enterprise platform for measuring and growing the return on investment of AI initiatives. Its Nucleus product connects workforce data and AI usage history to rank AI opportunities by impact, identify high-performing superusers, surface adoption gaps, and estimate time and cost savings. The company was co-founded by economists Erik Brynjolfsson (Stanford) and Andrew McAfee (MIT) with CEO James Milin and research director Daniel Rock (Wharton), is backed by Bloomberg Beta, and serves enterprise customers including Autodesk, Nasdaq, and LogicMonitor. Workhelix publishes no public API or developer program as of July 2026.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Widgera, Inc.
providers.description: Widgera is an AI-native business platform that unifies a company's operations into what it calls "One Adaptive OS." Its AI assistants (branded Aiva) learn a business, automate workflows, build internal apps, and run customer interactions across a suite of modules that includes CRM, Chats, Drive, Analytics, and autonomous Agents. Widgera positions itself as the infrastructure layer powering operations for retail, automotive, hospitality, real estate, and service organizations, with a roster of customers across consumer electronics retail, car service, real estate, and wellness. The company is backed by 500 Global. As of this profile Widgera runs a private application backend (api.widgera.com) but publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; its public surface is a marketing site plus Privacy and Terms pages and homepage-published compliance posture (SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR).

providers.name: Lyric
providers.description: Lyric is an AI-powered supply chain software company, founded in 2022 and backed by Insight Partners. Its Lyric Studio platform lets enterprises model, plan, and optimize their supply chains across four composable layers — Data (enterprise-grade data management and integrations), Algorithms (advanced supply chain science), Workflows (flexible, composable processes), and Models & Apps (ready-to-use applications). The platform spans network modeling, transportation optimization, inventory management, forecasting, routing, and scheduling. Lyric does not publish a public developer API surface; its product documentation at docs.lyric.tech is gated behind a Lyric Studio login. It does operate a public SafeBase security and trust portal documenting SOC 2, SOC 3, ISO/IEC 27001, GDPR, CCPA, CPRA, and CSA STAR Level 1 posture plus a responsible disclosure program.

providers.name: Datacor
providers.description: Datacor is an enterprise software company founded in 1981 and headquartered in Florham Park, New Jersey, that builds industry-specific business management and engineering software for process manufacturers, chemical distributors, and animal-nutrition producers. Its business-automation suite spans ERP, CRM, MES, WMS, formulation management, BLISS LIMS, regulatory and nutrition labeling, and TrackAbout asset tracking, while its engineering line delivers chemical process simulation and flow-modeling tools including CHEMCAD, Fathom, Arrow, Impulse, and xStream. Datacor serves the petrochemical, refinery, energy, feed, and specialty-chemical sectors, and has begun layering AI-driven capabilities across its products. The company is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. Datacor does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, or API specifications; this profile captures its verified public identity while the API surface (if any) remains behind its customer support portal.

providers.name: Kingsware
providers.description: Kingsware (Zhuhai Kingsware Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd. / 珠海金智维人工智能股份有限公司) is a leading Chinese enterprise AI and RPA solutions provider that builds "AI digital employees" and enterprise-grade agent platforms by fusing large language models, AI algorithms, and robotic process automation with vertical industry workflows. Its core products are the K-APA intelligent process automation (RPA) platform and the Ki-Agent enterprise agent platform (built around a "Supervised Agent" model with task planning, tool calling, multi-agent collaboration, and result verification), exposed through the Kingsware AI Open Platform (ai.kingsware.cn). The company serves finance, government, manufacturing, energy, telecom, education, HR, and finance/operations use cases; it has been recognized by IDC as the number-one China RPA+AI solution vendor by market share, counts all six major state-owned banks and 1,300+ enterprise/government customers, has deployed over 1.8 million AI digital employees, and is a national-level "little giant" (专精特新) enterprise. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: SunGard Data Systems
providers.description: SunGard Data Systems was a software and technology services company that provided software and processing solutions to financial services, education, and the public sector. In November 2015, SunGard was acquired by Fidelity National Information Services (FIS) for approximately $9.1 billion. Key product lines included SunGard Financial Systems (trading, treasury, risk management, capital markets), SunGard AvantGard (cash and liquidity management), SunGard K-12 (student information systems), and SunGard Higher Education (ERP for universities). Post-acquisition, these products were integrated into the FIS portfolio.

providers.name: CoPlane
providers.description: CoPlane is a San Francisco-based enterprise software company building an AI-native intelligent operations layer for the back office of essential enterprises. The platform combines AI agents with deterministic business rules on a durable workflow engine to automate high-friction, exception-heavy processes across finance, procurement, and operations — including invoice intake, PO matching, vendor onboarding, cash application, billing, collections, bank and account reconciliation, close processes, and variance analysis. CoPlane runs inside the customer's own cloud environment and interoperates with existing enterprise systems (SAP, Workday, Coupa) across Source-to-Pay, Quote-to-Cash, and Record-to-Report workflows without a rip-and-replace migration. Founded in 2024, the company raised a $14M seed round in November 2025 led by Ribbit Capital with participation from Stripe, Optum Ventures, and Terrain. This profile was surfaced as a Ribbit Capital portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; CoPlane does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Instalily
providers.description: InstaLILY builds Lily, an AI "Forward Deployed Engineer" for the physical and regulated economy. Lily learns how an enterprise operates, builds custom software agents for high-friction operational work such as quoting, routing, field service, and approvals, and runs them inside the systems companies already use including SAP, NetSuite, Epicor, Salesforce, HubSpot, and Snowflake. InstaLILY serves industrial distribution and MRO, manufacturing and OEM, field service, healthcare and pharma, and private equity. The company is headquartered at 455 Broadway, New York, and is backed by Insight Partners. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Reiner.ai
providers.description: Reiner.ai (operated by AI Mapping GmbH of Cologne, Germany) is a construction- and planning-industry AI platform for architects, engineers, and planners. It combines leading LLMs with domain-specific "Reiner Knowledge" and "Reiner Logic" layers to deliver Reiner Chat, task-specific KI-Agenten (AI agents) for site protocols, explanatory reports and project applications, company-knowledge integration, and a library of 50+ prebuilt construction prompts. The product is delivered as a hosted web application (app.reiner.ai); as of this enrichment pass there is no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Brain
providers.description: Brain Co. builds agent-native operating systems for institutions across the public and private sectors. Its Atlas platform powers GovOS — permitting, licensing, claims, and casework for government agencies at national scale — and InsuranceOS for underwriting, claims, authorization, and insurance operations, with an emphasis on sovereign-grade security and vendor neutrality. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, the company was cofounded by Elad Gil, Jared Kushner, and Luis Videgaray, with a team drawn from Google, DeepMind, NVIDIA, Palantir, and Tesla. Brain Co. does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI definitions; this profile tracks its public web surface (news, trust center, privacy and terms) pending any future developer program.

providers.name: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC)
providers.description: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC) is a leading American technology integrator providing full life cycle services and solutions in the technical, engineering, and enterprise information technology markets. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, SAIC serves the U.S. federal government with approximately $7.4 billion in annual revenues. The company delivers IT modernization, cloud computing, digital transformation, cybersecurity, AI/ML, and data analytics solutions primarily for defense, intelligence, and civilian government customers. SAIC's open source presence is at github.com/saic-oss with DevSecOps tools including Anvil (CI/CD container) and terraform modules for Kubernetes sandboxes.

providers.name: High Alpha
providers.description: High Alpha is a venture firm and venture studio based in Indianapolis, Indiana that creates and funds early-stage B2B SaaS companies. Through its Capital arm it makes pre-seed to Series B investments across the United States, and through its Studio it co-founds companies with entrepreneurs, providing design, brand, marketing, recruiting, product design, and go-to-market services. Founded by ExactTarget co-founder and CEO Scott Dorsey along with Eric Tobias, Mike Fitzgerald, and Studio Science founder Kristian Andersen, High Alpha pioneered the venture studio model and publishes the annual SaaS Benchmarks Report. Studio and portfolio companies include Salesloft, Lessonly, Attentive, Logik.ai, LogicGate, Dwolla, Zylo, and project44.

providers.name: Tiyaro
providers.description: Tiyaro is an enterprise AI company whose product, DeepQuery, replicates complete business processes as AI agents that can be described in plain English. Rather than rules engines or brittle integration workflows, DeepQuery uses LLMs combined with enterprise-specific product and customer data to identify a solution strategy and execute it across multiple steps using built-in tools. Its flagship application targets customer support and IT service desks - an "IT SuperAgent" trained on hundreds of third-party product procedures that recommends and executes resolution steps for incoming tickets - alongside revenue-operations and sales/marketing automation use cases. The company was founded by a team that previously built an edge software stack for hosting AI applications, and is backed by General Catalyst. Tiyaro goes to market as an enterprise product engaged through a book-a-demo motion rather than a self-serve developer API.

providers.name: Aravo
providers.description: Aravo Solutions is a San Francisco based enterprise software company providing third-party risk management (TPRM), supplier and procurement risk management, and governance, risk and compliance software. Its Intelligence First platform covers vendor nomination and intake, onboarding, due diligence, continuous monitoring, contracts, performance management, issue remediation and offboarding, with risk-domain applications for anti-bribery and corruption, data privacy and GDPR, information security, ESG, DORA and the German Supply Chain Due Diligence Act (LkSG). Aravo markets an integration framework that exchanges data with ERP, procure-to-pay, accounts payable and GRC systems, and with risk-intelligence providers including Refinitiv World-Check One, LexisNexis, Dow Jones, BitSight, SecurityScorecard, RapidRatings and Dun & Bradstreet, over SOAP and REST web-services APIs in XML and JSON. That API surface is described only on marketing pages; the reference documentation sits behind the login-gated Aravo customer portal.

providers.name: Newgen Software
providers.description: Newgen Software is a global provider of NewgenONE, a unified low-code digital transformation platform that orchestrates content services (enterprise content management), business process management (BPM/workflow), and customer communication management (CCM) for banks, insurers, government agencies, and healthcare organizations. Founded in 1992 and headquartered in New Delhi, India, the company is publicly listed (NSE/BSE) and serves enterprises worldwide with document management, intelligent document processing, case management, and process automation. Platform capabilities are exposed to customers and system integrators via REST APIs, but Newgen does not operate a public, self-service developer portal or publish OpenAPI/SDK artifacts on its marketing site.

providers.name: Schrödinger
providers.description: Schrödinger is a New York-headquartered (NASDAQ: SDGR) computational science company that develops a physics-based and AI-driven molecular simulation platform used across drug discovery and materials science. Its flagship desktop modeling environment is Maestro (MS Maestro for materials science), which integrates a deep stack of computational tools — Glide (docking), FEP+ (free energy perturbation), Desmond (molecular dynamics), Jaguar (quantum chemistry), Prime (protein structure prediction), BioLuminate (biologics), LigPrep, QikProp, SiteMap, and WaterMap — together with the Schrödinger-maintained PyMOL visualization system. LiveDesign is the cloud-native enterprise design lab where chemists, biologists, and program teams collaborate on molecules, run computational workflows, and integrate experimental data; it exposes a snap-in API framework for connecting in-house and third-party tooling. The Schrödinger Python API (current release 2026-1) is the primary developer surface, providing programmatic access to molecular structures, Maestro automation, jobcontrol, Glide, FEP+, Desmond, Jaguar, MacroModel, Prime, BioLuminate, and LiveDesign integration (login, export, dataset and column management). Schrödinger also ships KNIME extensions, command-line drivers for every computational product, and maintains a meaningful open-source footprint on GitHub — including PyMOL, maeparser, coordgenlibs, sketcher, gpusimilarity, csmiles, and the fixed-data-table-2 React component. The business has two segments — software licensing to global pharma, biotech, and materials companies, and a co-developed and proprietary drug discovery pipeline. There is no public developer signup or self-serve REST API; access to the platform, Python API, and LiveDesign is gated through commercial licensing and the my.schrodinger.com customer portal.

providers.name: Meta4
providers.description: Meta4 is a human capital management (HCM) software provider founded in Madrid, Spain, delivering cloud-based payroll, talent, and time-management applications widely used across the Spanish-speaking world and Europe. Backed by Insight Partners, Meta4 was acquired by Cegid in 2019 and its PeopleNet HCM platform is now delivered as part of the Cegid HR product family. The developer surface — Core HR, payroll, and talent APIs — is published through the Cegid HR developer portal rather than a standalone Meta4 developer program.

providers.name: B&L Information Systems
