providers.description: B&L Information Systems, LLC is a metalcasting-focused enterprise resource planning (ERP) software company founded more than 50 years ago and headquartered in Bridgman, Michigan. Its flagship product, Odyssey ERP, is a cloud-based ERP purpose-built for foundries, die casters, and investment casters, spanning manufacturing, sales, inventory, quality, finance, and data analytics. B&L pairs the software with implementation, consulting, data-conversion, training, and support services tailored to the metalcasting industry. The company is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. As of this enrichment pass, B&L does not publish a public developer portal, REST API documentation, SDKs, or an OpenAPI definition, so this profile captures company identity and public web properties rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Serviceware SE
providers.description: Serviceware SE is a German enterprise software, consulting, and managed-services company with more than 25 years in business, roughly 420 employees, and over EUR 100 million in annual revenue. Its platform spans Enterprise Service Management (ESM) for IT, HR, and customer service, IT Financial Management (ITFM) for cost tracking and technology business management, Corporate Performance Management (CPM) for budgeting, planning, and reporting, AI-powered Knowledge Management, and Field Service Management. Serviceware positions its platform as AI-native, with no-code workflows, data integration, governance, and self-service capabilities. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Spider Capital
providers.description: Spider Capital is a seed-stage venture capital firm investing in applied-AI enterprise cloud software that modernizes complex industrial sectors. The firm backs founders across construction, financial services, energy, government, healthcare, insurance, mining, manufacturing, supply chain, and transportation, citing 100+ enterprise cloud investments, a 70%+ seed-to-Series-A graduation rate, and portfolio companies including Mechanical Orchard, Imubit, CoLab, Percepto, Codoxo, Klir, Elara Spatial, and Logiwa. Surfaced as a portfolio company of foundry-group; it publishes no public API or developer surface (venture-capital firm), so this profile carries firm identity rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Cognizant Technology Solutions
providers.description: Cognizant Technology Solutions is a multinational information technology services and consulting company that provides digital, technology, consulting, and operations services to clients worldwide. Cognizant does not publish a general-purpose public REST API. Its developer-facing footprint is centered on the Cognizant Neuro AI platform family (Neuro AI Decisioning, Neuro AI Enterprise Core, Neuro AI Engineering, Neuro AI for IT Operations) and the open-source Neuro SAN multi-agent orchestration framework released by Cognizant AI Lab. Other delivered platforms (BigFrame for mainframe data migration, ADM accelerators, industry vertical solutions) are typically engaged via consulting engagements rather than self-service APIs.

providers.name: Kos
providers.description: Kos (Kosai, Inc.) builds what it calls the world's first virtual finance employee: an AI agent given its own workstation, org identity, software licenses, RBAC and audit logs, which completes finance and back-office workflows for capital- and inventory-heavy operators across datacenters, defense, energy, long-lead equipment, space and contracting. Kos reviews pay applications and vendor invoices line-by-line against GMP contracts, catching missing backup, overbills and calculation errors; generates, routes and closes out purchase orders inside a customer's ERP; and is taught new workflows over screenshare like a new hire. It is reached over email, Slack, Teams, phone and Zoom rather than through a UI, app or public API. Founded by Tanuj and Mani, who met as graduate researchers at Stanford under Sachin Katti; backed by 8VC, XYZ Ventures, MVP Ventures and Launch, with advisors including former Equinix CFO Keith Taylor. Headquartered in San Francisco, California.

providers.name: Edra
providers.description: Edra is an AI automation platform that analyzes an organization's existing business data - tickets, logs, messages, and system records - to automatically discover and document how operational processes actually run, then turns that knowledge into workflows that AI agents can execute reliably. The company targets knowledge-intensive functions such as IT service management and technical support, and integrates with common enterprise systems including ServiceNow, JIRA, Zendesk, Salesforce, and Outlook. Edra was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Edra publishes a corporate marketing site but no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Procuri
providers.description: Procuri (procuri.ai) presents itself as an AI-powered procurement automation platform that uses specialized AI agents to discover and vet suppliers, optimize contract negotiation and pricing, monitor policy and regulatory compliance, and assess supplier and market risk for enterprise procurement teams. It was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass the public site publishes no developer/API surface (no docs, developer, API-reference, or OpenAPI pages resolve).

providers.name: High Alpha Capital
providers.description: High Alpha is an Indianapolis-based venture firm that creates and funds B2B SaaS and enterprise software companies, partnering with founders through both a venture studio that co-creates companies from scratch and a capital arm that invests in early-stage enterprise software startups. Its focus spans healthcare, sales enablement, supply chain, agtech, and other B2B verticals, and its portfolio and alumni include companies such as Salesloft, Attentive, Lessonly, Stitch, Tenon, and Liminal. High Alpha also publishes the widely referenced SaaS Benchmarks Report. This profile tracks the firm in the API Evangelist network; as a venture firm it has no public developer or API surface of its own.

providers.name: Synaptic
providers.description: Synaptic is a vertical AI solutions company that extends Salesforce and Agentforce environments with pre-built, industry-specific AI agents and applications. Its AQ Platform ships purpose-built agents for healthcare payers and providers (Provider AQ), government citizen services (Citizen AQ), and high-tech customer service (Service AQ), using a value-first methodology that promises measurable results within 30 days and full implementation within 90 days. Synaptic is a managed-delivery solutions and consulting firm rather than a self-service developer platform; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or technical documentation. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Ribbit Capital.

providers.name: Bug Labs
providers.description: Bug Labs is a New York City enterprise software company founded in 2006, first as one of the earliest open-source modular hardware makers and later as an enterprise IoT platform provider serving Fortune 500 customers including Verizon, Comcast, VMware, Ford, Charter and Orange. Its current flagship product, Signalpattern, targets workflow fragmentation by mapping and connecting dispersed enterprise systems, automating cross-system tasks, and letting users interact with APIs directly without writing code. Bug Labs previously operated the well-known public IoT APIs dweet.io, dweetpro.io and freeboard.io; all three are decommissioned and the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation or public API today. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Spark Capital and Court Square Ventures.

providers.name: Fractal
providers.description: Fractal Software (fractalsoftware.com) is a venture studio that partners with entrepreneurs and investors to launch AI-driven vertical SaaS companies that transform how whole industries operate. Rather than shipping a single product, Fractal functions as an incubator and holding company, standing up sector-specific software startups across produce, healthcare, government, storage, distribution, and security-services verticals, with more than $650M raised across its portfolio. As a venture studio it exposes no public developer platform, API, SDKs, or documentation of its own; this profile captures its identity, portfolio surface, and domain-security posture. Note the recorded x-backed-by (multicoin, paradigm, a16z, 8vc) was surfaced via name-matching during portfolio ingestion and may conflate a distinct crypto-era "Fractal"; the enriched identity below reflects the fractalsoftware.com venture studio.

providers.name: ReadSoft
providers.description: ReadSoft was a provider of intelligent automation and business process management solutions for accounts payable and other document-intensive processes. Acquired by Lexmark in 2014, the technology was rolled into Kofax and is now part of Tungsten Automation. ReadSoft no longer publishes a public developer-facing REST API; its capture and AP automation products are delivered as installed enterprise software with partner-only integration resources.

providers.name: Digitalk
providers.description: Digitalk, Inc. was an American object-oriented software tools vendor and a Trinity Ventures portfolio company, best known for Smalltalk/V — a commercial Smalltalk development environment first released in 1986 for MS-DOS, preceded by "Digitalk Methods" in 1983. It was founded by George Bosworth, Jim Anderson, Mike Teng and Barbara Noparstak, and its product line grew into Visual Smalltalk Enterprise. In July 1995 Digitalk merged with its principal competitor ParcPlace Systems; the combined company was later renamed ObjectShare, announced a shift away from Smalltalk toward Java in 1997, and active development of the Digitalk line ended shortly after. The final release, Visual Smalltalk Enterprise 2000, shipped in September 2000. Cincom retains the right to sell and support VSE 2000 for existing licensees and Seagull Software owns the virtual machine. Digitalk predates the public web API era and operates no developer platform, public API, or live web presence today; this profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Alyne
providers.description: Alyne is a cloud-native governance, risk and compliance (GRC) platform, founded in Munich in 2015 and acquired by Mitratech in 2021, where it is now offered as Mitratech's Alyne. The platform pairs a large curated library of controls and regulatory content with AI-assisted risk assessments, control mapping, maturity scoring and reporting, helping enterprises and FinTechs manage cyber, operational and third-party risk. Alyne is delivered as SaaS through app.alyne.com and is positioned to integrate with common IT, compliance and data systems. As of this profile Alyne exposes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI definition; this record captures its public identity and probed domain security.

providers.name: Broadvision
providers.description: BroadVision spans two chapters of Dr. Pehong Chen's technology work. BroadVision, Inc. (NASDAQ: BVSN), founded in 1993 and backed by Mayfield, was a pioneer of e-commerce and enterprise self-service portal software and later the Vmoso enterprise collaboration platform; the operating company was acquired by ESW Capital in 2020. The broadvision.com domain is now home to BroadVision Group (BVG), a US-based private asset management firm formed in 2006 that funds, incubates, and operates ventures across artificial intelligence, cleantech, fintech, healthtech, biotech, medtech, semiconductors, and cloud/big-data. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Fabrion
providers.description: Fabrion builds an AI Operating System for industrial manufacturers, applying artificial intelligence to manufacturing operations and the industrial sector. The company is a venture-backed portfolio company of 8vc and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As of this enrichment pass Fabrion publishes a marketing website with AI Lab, Careers, and Contact pages, but exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, packages, MCP server, or other machine-readable developer artifacts. No developer, docs, or api subdomains resolve and no /.well-known/, llms.txt, pricing, or blog surfaces were found. This remains a lead awaiting a real API surface to enrich against.

providers.name: Leidos
providers.description: Leidos, a Fortune 500 digital and mission innovator, delivers solutions at the intersection of national security, health, and critical infrastructure. With a global workforce of approximately 47,000, the company is executing its NorthStar 2030 strategy focused on five growth engines: space and maritime, energy infrastructure, digital modernization and cyber, mission software, and managed health. No public REST APIs or developer portal have been identified.

providers.name: Baan
providers.description: Baan (Baan Company N.V., originally The Baan Corporation) was a Dutch enterprise resource planning software vendor founded in 1978 in Barneveld, Netherlands by Jan Baan and later joined by his brother Paul Baan. Baan built one of the first genuinely component-based ERP suites, known for its Dynamic Enterprise Modeler (DEM), its Baan Tools 4GL development environment, and deep manufacturing and project-industry functionality. At its late-1990s peak Baan served roughly 3,000 customers and posted close to $700 million in revenue, making it one of the leading global ERP providers alongside SAP, Oracle and PeopleSoft. Following accounting controversy and a collapse in its share price, Baan was acquired by the British engineering group Invensys in 2000, sold on to SSA Global Technologies in 2003, and absorbed into Infor Global Solutions when Infor acquired SSA in 2006. Baan no longer exists as an operating company or an independent brand: the product line lives on as Infor LN, and the baan.com and baan.nl domains now permanently redirect to the Infor LN product page. Consequently this profile carries no first-party API surface of its own — any modern programmatic access to the Baan lineage is delivered through Infor LN REST APIs and the Infor ION API gateway on Infor's developer platform. Baan Company is listed by Battery Ventures as an exited investment.

providers.name: Doczen
providers.description: Doczen is an enterprise AI transformation platform that connects business signals to actionable outcomes, helping large organizations adopt AI in days rather than months. The product uses AI agents to interview employees and aggregate signals from communication and productivity tools to surface operational issues, then ranks the resulting opportunities by financial impact, ROI, feasibility, and urgency. It guides implementation through buy-vs-build decisions and vendor recommendations, and runs a continuous monitoring loop that tracks progress and measures business impact. Doczen targets enterprises across financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, energy, technology, and transportation and logistics, and integrates with hundreds of tools. It advertises an enterprise security and compliance posture (ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR, EU AI Act) via a Vanta-hosted trust center. Doczen is backed by Seedcamp and was added to the API Evangelist network from the Seedcamp portfolio; it currently exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Lab0
providers.description: Lab0 (lab0.ai) is a San Francisco company in the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch building an "AI forward-deployed engineer" for B2B SaaS: agentic systems that automate enterprise software implementation and post-sales delivery. The platform runs discovery, solution design, configuration, custom integration build, testing and go-live in parallel, with the stated goal of compressing 3-12 month deployment cycles down to weeks. Its connector agents profile a customer instance (tables, fields, auth model, processes) to produce a connector spec, then generate the integration, auth, field mappings, callbacks and write-back workflows as staged changes a human team reviews, with every write previewed as a controlled dry-run before it touches the customer instance. Named target systems are ServiceNow, SAP, Salesforce, Workday and Adobe AEM, plus custom APIs. As of this profile Lab0 is pre-launch as a developer platform: it publishes a marketing site and an llms.txt, but no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or self-serve sign-up. It is sold as a managed engagement via founder contact and demo booking.

providers.name: LikeWise
providers.description: Likewise Software was a Bellevue, Washington enterprise software company building storage, identity and security products that bridged Linux, Unix and Mac systems into Microsoft Active Directory environments. Its OEM line, Likewise Storage Services, supplied SMB/CIFS multi-protocol file access to network storage vendors including HP StorageWorks, Riverbed, EMC Data Domain and NetApp, while Likewise Data Analytics and Governance covered auditing, reporting and compliance (HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX, FISMA) over unstructured data. Its Likewise Enterprise and Likewise Open Active Directory integration products moved to BeyondTrust. Backed by Trinity Ventures, the company was acquired and no longer operates: there is no live website, developer portal, documentation or public API, and the likewise.com domain now redirects to an unrelated owner.

providers.name: Tivoli
providers.description: Tivoli Systems was an Austin, Texas systems-management software company founded in 1989 that helped enterprises manage distributed client/server networks of PCs and workstations. After a 1995 NASDAQ IPO (TIVS), IBM acquired Tivoli in March 1996 for approximately $743 million, and it became the IBM Tivoli enterprise systems and network management brand before IBM retired the name and folded its products into other IBM software lines. A historic Norwest venture exit, Tivoli no longer exists as an independent company and publishes no independent API surface; tivoli.com is an IBM-held domain that redirects toward ibm.com.

providers.name: Utopia Technology Partners
providers.description: Utopia Technology Partners, Inc. was a help desk software and IT support services company based in Larkspur, California, backed by Battery Ventures (listed as an exited investment). It was acquired by Royalblue Group plc of Woking, UK on May 11, 1998, expanding Royalblue's US help desk operation to the West Coast. The company is defunct - its California corporate registration is suspended and it publishes no website, developer portal, or API surface.

providers.name: Hang Ten
providers.description: Hang Ten Systems is an enterprise AI services company founded in 2026 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. Led by co-founder and CEO Dr. Vishal Sikka (formerly CEO of Infosys and a member of SAP's executive board), the company helps large enterprises adopt AI to build, change, and run the software that runs their business at a fraction of the cost and time. Its AI-native delivery model combines agentic code generation, a reusable skills library, and deep domain expertise across SAP migrations, finance, HR, and new product development. Hang Ten raised a $32 million seed round led by Mayfield with strategic investment from Aramco Ventures, and counts Siemens Gamesa Renewable Energy and Fresenius among its early customers.

providers.name: Nova
providers.description: Nova (Nova Intelligence) is an agentic AI platform for SAP teams, used in production across documentation, functional design, development, and production issue resolution. Its capabilities include code intelligence and system visibility, fit-to-standard analysis mapping custom code to SAP standard, development acceleration for ABAP Cloud and BTP CAP, S/4HANA and Clean Core transformation support, and security vulnerability identification, with claims of a 3x productivity boost at 50% lower cost. Nova is an enterprise, demo-led product with no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time; it is backed by Accel and Battery Ventures. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which probed the company's public surface and found a domain-security posture and a Vanta trust center but no developer or API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Alight
providers.description: Alight is a leading cloud-based human capital and technology services provider that powers confident health, wealth, and wellbeing decisions for millions of employees and family members. The company delivers integrated benefits administration, payroll, and total wellbeing solutions through its Alight Worklife platform. Alight does not publish a public, self-service developer portal; integrations are typically delivered through enterprise client engagements.

providers.name: acorn systems
providers.description: Acorn is a Time-Driven Activity-Based Costing (TD-ABC) and profitability-management platform for multi-dimensional cost-to-serve analysis, precisely attributing direct and indirect costs against products, customers, regions, business units and facilities. It offers what-if scenario modeling, shared-services optimization, custom business-process modeling, and OLAP/analytics for pricing, supplier negotiation and supply-chain decisions. Originally Acorn Systems, the product is now owned and operated by IgniteTech (an ESW Capital enterprise-software company); the acornsys.com domain 301-redirects into IgniteTech's software library. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification is published for the product.

providers.name: Aelita Software
providers.description: Aelita Software Corporation was an enterprise systems-management software company founded in 1998 by Ratmir Timashev (who later co-founded Veeam Software). Headquartered in the Columbus, Ohio area (Dublin/Powell, OH), Aelita built Windows infrastructure management tooling for Microsoft Active Directory and Microsoft Exchange environments — including migration, directory management, auditing, reporting, security analysis, systems monitoring, and disaster recovery. Marquee products included Migration Manager for Active Directory, Migration Manager for Exchange, Secure Copy, Enterprise Reporter, Recovery Manager for Active Directory, ActiveRoles Server, and InTrust. Insight Partners was an early investor. Aelita was acquired by Quest Software in March 2004 for approximately $115 million and its technology was folded into Quest's Windows Management line (much of which is now part of One Identity). The company has had no independent operation since 2004; it exposed no public developer API, developer portal, or documentation surface, and there is no live web presence today (the aelita.com domain is parked/for sale). This profile is retained as a historical Insight Partners portfolio record — there is no active developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Agile Software
providers.description: Agile Software Corporation was an American product lifecycle management (PLM) software company founded in 1995 and headquartered in San Jose, California. Backed by Accel, it IPO'd on the NASDAQ in 1999 and built enterprise software that helped manufacturers manage product records, bills of materials, engineering change orders, quality, compliance, and supply-chain data across a product's development and production lifecycle. Oracle Corporation acquired Agile Software in July 2007 for approximately US$495 million; its products were rebranded as Oracle Agile PLM and folded into Oracle's supply-chain and applications suite. The company no longer operates independently: agilesoft.com now redirects to Oracle, and the only surviving developer surface is the legacy Oracle Agile PLM SDK (a Java API set) hosted on docs.oracle.com. This profile is retained as an acquired/historical record; there is no live, independent public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Airware
providers.description: Airware was an enterprise commercial-drone (UAV) software and aerial-data-analytics company founded in 2011 by Jonathan Downey and headquartered in San Francisco. It began by building an operating system and autopilot for commercial drones, then pivoted to a cloud-based "Aerial Information Platform" that captured, processed, and analyzed drone imagery for enterprise verticals such as mining, quarrying, insurance, and construction. Airware acquired French drone-analytics firm Redbird in 2016 and raised roughly $118M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Kleiner Perkins, GV (Google Ventures), Intel Capital, and Next World Capital. The company ceased operations in September 2018. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; no live developer surface, API, or public specification is currently discoverable (the airware.com domain no longer resolves), so this profile is retained as a historical/defunct record.

providers.name: Alpharel
providers.description: Alpharel, Inc. was a Camarillo, California document-management and imaging company founded in 1981 that built turnkey digital document transmission and management systems (scanners, optical disks, terminals, LANs) for industrial, commercial, and government use. It acquired Optigraphics in 1993, renamed itself Altris Software in October 1996, and its business was ultimately succeeded by Spescom Software, Inc. of San Diego. Alpharel appears in the Battery Ventures portfolio list. The company is DEFUNCT under this name: it has no active first-party website, developer portal, API, or SDKs, so there is no API/developer surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: Applimation
providers.description: Applimation was a provider of application Information Lifecycle Management (ILM) and enterprise data archiving software for packaged applications including SAP (ERP, HR, CRM, SRM, SCM, APO) and Oracle environments, helping customers manage the full data lifecycle from test-data management through archiving of inactive data to lower storage and database costs and improve application performance. Informatica acquired Applimation for approximately $40 million in an agreement announced in February 2009, folding its ILM and database-archiving technology into Informatica's data management portfolio. Applimation no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer surface, API, or documentation.

providers.name: Arbor Software
providers.description: Arbor Software Corporation was an enterprise business-intelligence and OLAP software company founded in 1991 in Sunnyvale, California by Bob Earle and Jim Dorian. It created Essbase, the pioneering multidimensional online-analytical-processing (OLAP) server first released in 1992, and went public on NASDAQ under the ticker ARSW in 1995. Arbor merged with Hyperion Software in 1998 to form Hyperion Solutions Corporation, which Oracle Corporation acquired in 2007; the Essbase technology lives on inside Oracle. Arbor Software no longer exists as an independent entity and publishes no live API, developer portal, or documentation surface, so there is nothing to enrich.

providers.name: BackWeb
providers.description: BackWeb Technologies Ltd. was an Israeli-American enterprise software company founded in 1995 by Eli Barkat, Nir Barkat, Yuval Rakavy, Iftah Sneh and Lior Hass, with offices in Ramat Gan, Israel and San Jose, California. BackWeb pioneered "Polite" push technology — background delivery of software updates, patches, alerts and marketing content to desktops using only idle bandwidth so it did not disrupt the user or the corporate network. Its Polite Communication Server, Offline Access Server, e-Accelerator and Proactive Portal products were deployed by Cisco, Hewlett-Packard, IBM, Ericsson, Compaq and SAP, and integrators used the BackWeb Server Extension API and BackWeb Automation SDK to publish content from external data sources into the Polite server. The company IPO'd on NASDAQ (BWEB) in June 1999 after raising roughly $13M privately from investors including Goldman Sachs, Intel and Trinity Ventures, peaking near $38M in annual revenue. It never recovered from the dot-com collapse, was delisted from NASDAQ and moved to the OTC Bulletin Board, approved a voluntary liquidation in 2012, suspended operations and divested its patents in 2014, and began distributing remaining cash to shareholders. BackWeb is defunct: there is no operating company, no developer portal, and no live API. The backweb.com domain is a parked Afternic for-sale lander. This profile is retained as a historical record only.

providers.name: Bebop
providers.description: Bebop (bebop.co) was a stealth-mode enterprise software startup founded by Diane Greene, co-founder and former CEO of VMware, building a development platform intended to make it easier to build and maintain enterprise applications. The company never shipped a public product, developer portal, or API, and was acquired by Google on November 19, 2015 for approximately $380 million, at which point Diane Greene was named head of Google's newly consolidated enterprise cloud business (Google for Work, Cloud Platform, and Google Apps). The acquired technology was later folded into Google Hire, which Google shut down in 2019. Bebop is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical a16z portfolio record; it has no live domain, no public API surface, and no developer artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Bluedata Software Inc
providers.description: BlueData Software Inc was a big-data infrastructure company whose EPIC platform ran Hadoop, Spark, and other analytics workloads in Docker containers on-premises and in the cloud. It was a dcvc (Data Collective) portfolio company and was acquired by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) in 2018; its technology now lives on as the HPE Ezmeral Container Platform. The original www.bluedata.com domain 301-redirects to HPE's container-platform page, and the company no longer operates an independent developer, API, or documentation surface, so there is nothing for the enrichment pipeline to harvest without fabrication. This profile is retained as an acquired-company lead.

providers.name: Calista Technologies
providers.description: Calista Technologies was a desktop and GPU virtualization startup founded in 2006 in San Jose, California by Neal Margulis, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Greylock, and Western Technology Investment. Its software improved the user experience of 3-D and multimedia delivery for virtualized desktop deployments and server-hosted applications running on Windows Server Terminal Services (Remote Desktop). Microsoft acquired the company in 2008 and folded its GPU-virtualization technology into RemoteFX. The company is defunct and publishes no live developer, documentation, or API surface; its former domain (calistatechnologies.com) is now a parked domain listed for sale.

providers.name: CenterForce Technologies
providers.description: CenterForce Technologies was a Bethesda, Maryland software company that built workforce-optimization, workforce-management, and performance-analytics software for contact centers. It partnered with Concerto Software for nearly a decade before Concerto acquired it on 2004-04-26 to pair CenterForce's workforce and contact-center management tools with Concerto's ACD, IVR, and email contact-channel products. Concerto was itself taken private in 2005 and rebranded as Aspect Software in 2007, absorbing the former CenterForce workforce-optimization product line. The company raised roughly $6.01M; investors included Battery Ventures, Piper Sandler, Aspect Software, and SightLine Partners. It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio lead. Enrichment (2026-07-18) confirmed it is a long-defunct, acquired entity with no independent website, developer portal, or API surface; there is nothing to catalog.

providers.name: Chordiant Software
providers.description: Chordiant Software Corporation was an enterprise software vendor founded in 1991 and based in California, known for customer relationship management (CRM) and customer decision management software used by large banks, insurers, telecommunications carriers, and healthcare organizations. Its products included Chordiant Decision Management, Marketing Director, and Recommendation Advisor, delivering real-time predictive decisioning and next-best-action recommendations across customer channels. The company went public on NASDAQ (CHRD) in 2000 and was acquired by Pegasystems in 2010, with its decisioning technology folded into Pega's Customer Decision Hub. Chordiant no longer operates as an independent company and exposes no public developer portal or API; the chordiant.com domain now redirects to pega.com. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record and carries no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: ConnectCapital
providers.description: ConnectCapital is a private equity investment firm, established in 2000, that made investments in early and expansion stage companies providing enterprise application and infrastructure software and solutions. It was surfaced as a portfolio entry of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating web presence - the connectcapital.com domain is parked on GoDaddy nameservers and redirects every path to a lander, and connect-capital.com is listed for sale. ConnectCapital is an investor, not an API producer, and has no developer portal, documentation, or API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Consona
providers.description: Consona Corporation was an Indianapolis, Indiana enterprise software company founded in 1986 as Made2Manage Systems and taken private by Battery Ventures in 2003. Operating a roll-up strategy, it acquired multiple ERP and CRM product lines (DTR, Cimnet, AXIS, Encompix, Intuitive, Relevant, SupplyWorks) serving small and midsize manufacturers and field-service businesses. On August 7, 2012 Consona merged with CDC Software to form Aptean, and the Consona brand was retired from commercial use. The company is defunct, has no live web domain (consona.com does not resolve) and no public API or developer surface; its former products live on inside Aptean.

providers.name: Corio, Inc.
providers.description: Corio, Inc. was an enterprise Application Service Provider (ASP) founded in September 1998 in San Carlos, California, and incorporated in Delaware, formed by acquiring the capital stock of Data Systems Connectors, Inc. Corio implemented, hosted and managed packaged enterprise business software from Oracle, PeopleSoft, SAP, Ariba and Siebel Systems on behalf of medium and large public, private, non-profit and public sector customers, delivering ERP, CRM and e-business functionality as a service from secure third-party data centers over IP networks. The company operated two lines of business — Application Management Services and Professional Services — and partnered with (i)Structure, XO Communications and Qwest for data center and network infrastructure. Backed by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers (29.5% pre-IPO across the KPCB Java Fund, KPCB VIII, KPCB VIII Founders Fund and KPCB Information Sciences Zaibatsu Fund II, with Vinod Khosla and Ted Schlein on the board) and Cap Gemini Ernst & Young, Corio went public on NASDAQ in 2000. IBM agreed to acquire Corio on 24 January 2005 for $2.82 per share in cash via Nike Acquisition Corp.; Corio filed its Form 15 deregistration on 15 March 2005 and was absorbed into IBM. The company is defunct, publishes no API, developer portal or documentation, and corio.com is a parked domain — there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Cross Access
providers.description: Cross Access was a data-integration software company backed by Battery Ventures that was acquired by IBM on 2003-10-17 and folded into IBM's information-integration portfolio. It is defunct and has no independent web presence, developer portal, API, or documentation surface today; DNS for candidate domains (crossaccess.com, cross-access.com, crossaccess.io) does not resolve. This profile is retained as a historical Battery Ventures portfolio record, not an active API provider, and there are no live artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: CubeTree
providers.description: CubeTree was an enterprise social collaboration software startup (founded 2008, Redwood City, California) offering a business social network with wikis, blogs, file sharing, and activity feeds. It was acquired by SuccessFactors in 2010 (deal valued up to $50M) and folded into the SuccessFactors Business Alignment suite; SAP subsequently acquired SuccessFactors in 2012 and the product was absorbed into SAP SuccessFactors / SAP Jam. CubeTree no longer operates as an independent company: the cubetree.com domain is parked under SAP nameservers with no live web presence, developer portal, documentation, or API. Surfaced as a trinity-ventures portfolio company; retained as a historical/defunct network record with no enrichable API surface.

providers.name: Cullinet Software
providers.description: Cullinet Software (formerly Cullinane Database Systems) was a database and application software company based in Westwood, Massachusetts, best known for the IDMS/IDMS-DB mainframe database management system, the IDD data dictionary, and the ADS/Online application development environment for IBM mainframes. Backed by Battery Ventures, Greylock, and Morgenthaler Ventures, it was one of the first software companies to go public (1978) and was acquired by Computer Associates (CA) on June 30, 1989. The company is defunct and publishes no developer portal, API, or documentation surface today; this record is retained as a historical portfolio-graph node with no enrichable API artifacts.

providers.name: DecisionPoint Software
providers.description: DecisionPoint Software was a San Mateo, California-based enterprise software company that provided packaged financial performance management (FPM) and financial data warehousing software, built primarily around the Oracle ERP stack. Its systems captured and moved continuously changing data from financial source systems into a data warehouse, automatically configuring the analytic environment as the source systems changed, and shipped as far as Release 11 with operations in both the United States and the United Kingdom. The company was named one of the 50 fastest-growing private companies in Silicon Valley in 2004 and raised a $5M Series B round from Battery Ventures that same year. It was acquired in December 2005 by NCR's Teradata data warehousing division, which folded the FPM and data warehousing technology into the Teradata enterprise data warehouse offering. DecisionPoint Software has not operated as an independent company for roughly two decades: it publishes no website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface, and this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Deployco
providers.description: Deployco (the OpenAI Deployment Company, DeployCo) is a ~$10B enterprise-AI joint venture launched by OpenAI in May 2026 to help organizations put frontier AI into production. It is an engineering-heavy consulting and deployment business: Forward Deployed Engineers and Deployment Specialists embed in client companies to connect OpenAI models to their data, tools, controls, and core workflows (RAG, fine-tuning/distillation, infrastructure, and safety/compliance). It is backed by a founding-investor group including Emergence Capital. DeployCo is a services/consulting entity and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, OpenAPI spec, or SDKs of its own; any API surface it uses is the OpenAI platform. No API artifacts are available to enrich at this time.

providers.name: Digital Market
providers.description: Digital Market was an enterprise-software company that built electronic-components B2B commerce software, backed by Trinity Ventures. It was acquired by Agile Software and no longer operates as an independent provider. It is not an API provider and publishes no live developer surface, documentation, or specifications; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio record rather than an active, enrichable API.

providers.name: Dirig Software
providers.description: Dirig Software, Inc. was a Nashua, New Hampshire software company that built application and system management software for eBusiness — agent-based performance monitoring and automated problem correction for J2EE application servers (WebLogic, WebSphere), web infrastructure, and hosted service-provider environments, sold both direct to enterprises and through OEM and service-provider channels. The company was venture-backed by Battery Ventures. Its web presence at dirig.com carried full product, partner, and support content through roughly 2003, degraded to a broken holding page under the name "Dirig Corporation" from early 2004, and by late 2006 the domain was a parked Sedo for-sale page. As of this enrichment pass the company has no live website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface of any kind; dirig.com now resolves to an unrelated third-party endpoint returning a bare "OK" health response. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network — there is nothing to enrich and nothing to score.

providers.name: Fuego
providers.description: Fuego, Inc. (maker of FuegoBPM) was an enterprise business process management (BPM) and service-oriented architecture software company founded circa 1999 in Plano, Texas. It was backed by Trinity Ventures among others (Series A, 2004) and was acquired by BEA Systems in March 2006, where FuegoBPM became the basis of BEA AquaLogic BPM; BEA was subsequently acquired by Oracle in 2008 and the technology folded into the Oracle BPM product line. Fuego no longer exists as an independent company and publishes no live website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface.

providers.name: I2 Technologies Inc (THINK SYSTEMS)
providers.description: i2 Technologies Inc was a Dallas-based supply-chain management software company founded in 1988 by Sanjiv Sidhu and Ken Sharma; "THINK SYSTEMS" refers to Think Systems Inc, a supply-chain planning software firm i2 acquired in 1997. i2 Technologies was itself acquired by JDA Software in 2010, which rebranded to Blue Yonder in 2020 and is now owned by Panasonic. This is a defunct/historical entity with no independent, live developer or API surface. The enrichment pass found no attributable API to enrich; the live i2group.com intelligence-analysis APIs belong to a different, unrelated company (a name collision), and the "insight-partners" backing appears to be an erroneous VC-portfolio match.

providers.name: iceonline
providers.description: iceonline (冰场联盟) operates an enterprise-grade backend management platform for ice rinks in China, published at www.iceonline.cn as a login-gated single-page administrative console branded "冰场联盟 企业级后台管理系统" (Ice Rink Alliance Enterprise Management System). The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the public surface is a private SPA with no discoverable API: no OpenAPI/Swagger, SDK, developer portal, changelog, or security.txt was found — every probed path (including /.well-known/*, /swagger.json, /openapi.json) returns the SPA shell rather than a real document. Only live domain-security posture (TLS/DNS) could be captured this round.

providers.name: Identify Software
providers.description: Identify Software Ltd. was an Israeli enterprise-software company founded in 1996 in Petah Tikva by Yochi Slonim, backed by earlybird (invested 2001). It built application performance management, software-testing, and business-process-automation tooling that helped IT teams reproduce, diagnose, and resolve production application problems, best known for its AppSight problem-resolution suite. It is a legacy portfolio entry rather than an active API provider: the identify.software domain is parked/for-sale, there is no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to enrich, so this profile is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead only.

providers.name: Illustra
providers.description: Illustra Information Technologies was an object-relational database company founded in 1992 by Michael Stonebraker, Gary Morgenthaler and several of Stonebraker's students to commercialize the Postgres research project. Its DataBlade extensibility modules let structured and unstructured multimedia data (text, geospatial, web content) be stored and indexed as true objects. NASA selected it in 1995 to store millions of satellite images. Informix Corporation acquired the company in 1996 and folded the object-relational engine and DataBlades into what became Informix Universal Server; that lineage passed to IBM and is now maintained by HCL Technologies. Illustra no longer exists as an independent entity and publishes no standalone website, developer portal, or API. This record was surfaced from a historical Trinity Ventures portfolio list; enrichment found no live API surface.

providers.name: Intraware
providers.description: Intraware, Inc. was a software delivery and entitlement-management company founded in 1996 and headquartered in Orinda, California. Its flagship SubscribeNet service gave enterprise software publishers a web-based electronic software delivery (ESD) and license-management platform, delivering applications through an encryption, compression, and multi-server distribution engine while giving corporate IT subscribers account-specific entitlement, update, and download information. Intraware went public on NASDAQ under the ticker ITRA in 1999 during the dot-com boom, was backed by investors including Canaan Partners, and was acquired in 2009 by Acresso Software (later Flexera Software). Its SubscribeNet software-monetization capabilities live on today as part of Revenera; there is no independent Intraware developer program, public API, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a Canaan Partners portfolio company and is retained as a historical VC-portfolio lead.

providers.name: Kiva Software
providers.description: Kiva Software Corporation was a pioneer of the internet application server, founded in May 1994 by chairman and CEO Keng Lim and headquartered in Mountain View, California. In January 1996 Kiva shipped what is widely credited as the industry's first web application server, giving companies a platform for developing and deploying transaction-oriented business applications on the web — and the first Java application server to market, with C++ application development supported alongside it. The product line comprised the Kiva Enterprise Server (deployment and management runtime), the Kiva Application Builder (graphical development tool), and the Kiva SDK with Java and C++ foundation classes; the company also ran the Kiva Enterprise Alliance Program (KEAP) for end-to-end partner solutions. Customers included Bank of America, E-Trade, Travelocity, Internet Shopping Network, Hong Kong Telecom, and Pacific Bell Internet. Kiva raised roughly $13.9 million across two rounds from Weiss Peck & Greer, Greylock, Discovery Ventures, Sippl MacDonald Ventures, Norwest Venture Capital, and Trinity Ventures, and is listed in the Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio as a 1996 early-stage investment. In December 1997 Netscape Communications acquired Kiva for approximately $180 million in stock (6.3 million Netscape shares), and the Kiva Enterprise Server became the Netscape Application Server — which went on to become the iPlanet Application Server under the AOL/Netscape–Sun Microsystems alliance, then Sun ONE Application Server and Sun Java System Application Server. Kiva has not operated independently since 1997, published no public developer API in the modern sense, and has no live web presence today (the historical www.kivasoft.com domain is now parked and listed for sale). This profile is retained as a historical Lightspeed and Trinity Ventures portfolio record — there is no active developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Legato Systems
providers.description: Legato Systems, Inc. was a storage management software company founded in 1988 in Palo Alto, California by four former Sun Microsystems engineers — Jon Kepecs, Bob Lyon, Joe Moran, and Russell Sandberg. Its flagship product, NetWorker, was introduced for Unix in 1990 and became one of the defining enterprise backup, recovery, and archiving platforms of the client-server era, centralizing scheduled backup, media management, and disaster recovery across heterogeneous Unix, Windows, and NetWare environments. Backed by Mayfield, the company went public in July 1995. EMC Corporation announced its acquisition of Legato in July 2003 and completed it in October 2003 for an estimated $1.3 billion, folding the product line into EMC's information-management portfolio. NetWorker survives today as Dell EMC NetWorker following Dell's 2016 acquisition of EMC. No Legato-branded developer or API surface remains: the legato.com domain carries Akamai nameservers but publishes no website, and the company predates modern package registries, so no first-party client libraries exist. This profile is retained as a historical Mayfield portfolio record.

providers.name: MCA Solutions
providers.description: MCA Solutions was a service parts planning and optimization software company founded in 1999 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Its Service Planning and Optimization (SPO) suite helped aerospace and defense, high-tech, and capital-equipment firms reduce spare-parts inventory, lower support costs, and improve service levels across the service supply chain. Backed by Battery Ventures and Longworth Venture Partners, the company was acquired by Marlin Equity Partners in March 2012 and merged into Servigistics (later part of PTC). It no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live website, developer portal, or API surface.

providers.name: Metalogix
providers.description: Metalogix was an independent software vendor providing migration, management, and security solutions for Microsoft SharePoint and Office 365, best known for its Content Matrix SharePoint-to-SharePoint migration tool. Quest Software acquired Metalogix in June 2018, and the metalogix.com domain now redirects to Quest, where the products live on as the Metalogix Content Matrix line. The tooling is delivered as a desktop console with PowerShell cmdlets that drive the supported SharePoint APIs; it does not publish an independent public REST API, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, or client SDK. This profile is retained for network/portfolio lineage.

providers.name: Net Effect Systems
providers.description: Net Effect Systems is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: enterprise-software. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: O11
providers.description: O11 is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building custom AI software for financial services firms. Rather than forcing teams onto a new external platform, O11 embeds AI-driven automation directly into the tools finance teams already use every day — Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and other enterprise applications — so users can generate presentations, spreadsheets, and documents and automate workflows without switching contexts. The company positions itself against the observation that a majority of firms still rely on legacy software where generic bolt-on AI features fail to deliver real value. As of this profile O11 publishes a marketing site (o11.ai) but no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation could be found; this remains an early-stage identity profile in the API Evangelist network awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: OFF
providers.description: OFF (Off-Live, off.live) is an enterprise AI software company building intelligent applications that help organizations streamline, innovate, and grow. Its products include AiVee, a smart scheduling assistant that uses computer vision to turn calendar images into digital events and manage invitations across popular calendar apps, and Pumky, a text-to-image generation platform with customizable artistic styles for both beginners and professionals. The company builds on computer vision, multilingual large language models, and domain-specialized AI models. Backed by Coinbase Ventures, Samsung Next, and Electric Capital. Surfaced as a portfolio company of electric-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Orative
providers.description: Orative Corporation was an enterprise software company that built conferencing and collaboration software for mobile business users, offering a client-server product to manage conversations, collaborate with colleagues, filter unwanted calls and notifications, and access personal and corporate directories. Founded in the early 2000s, it raised a $12M Series B in July 2004 led by Trinity Ventures (with Mayfield and Diamondhead Ventures) and was acquired by Cisco Systems in October 2006. The company is defunct: there is no live product, developer portal, or API surface today. This profile was surfaced as a Trinity Ventures portfolio company and processed by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline, which confirmed no current API surface exists.

providers.name: Primavera Systems
providers.description: Primavera Systems, Inc. was a project-management and project-portfolio-management software company best known for the Primavera P6 scheduling platform used in construction, engineering, and capital-projects industries. It was acquired by Oracle Corporation in 2008 and folded into Oracle's Construction and Engineering business, where the products live on as Oracle Primavera. As an independent company it no longer exists, its primavera.com domain now redirects to oracle.com/primavera, and it publishes no independent public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation of its own. This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead, but that association does not match the acquired-by-Oracle entity and appears to be a name-matching artifact.

providers.name: Quest Software Inc.
providers.description: Quest Software Inc. is a privately held IT management and cybersecurity software company headquartered in Aliso Viejo, California. Its portfolio spans database management and development (Toad), database and infrastructure performance monitoring (Foglight, Spotlight), unified endpoint management (KACE), Microsoft platform management and security (On Demand, Change Auditor, Recovery Manager, Migration Manager), data protection and backup (NetVault, QoreStor, Rapid Recovery), data replication (SharePlex), and data governance and modeling (erwin). Its products are distributed and supported through the Quest Support portal. Surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub and processed by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; no public, first-party developer API portal or OpenAPI surface was discoverable at enrichment time.

providers.name: Remedy Corporation
providers.description: Remedy Corporation was an IT service management (ITSM) software company founded in 1991 by Lawrence Garlick, David Mahler, and Doug Mueller, and backed by Accel with a Series A investment. Its flagship Action Request System (AR System) became a leading help-desk and IT service management platform. The company went public on NASDAQ under the ticker RMDY, was acquired by Peregrine Systems in 2001, and its ITSM assets were subsequently acquired by BMC Software in 2002, where the Remedy ITSM product line continued for many years. Remedy Corporation no longer exists as an independent company and publishes no active developer portal, documentation, or public API.

providers.name: Rowspace
providers.description: Rowspace builds AI infrastructure for major asset managers, converting fragmented institutional knowledge into clean, structured data that AI can reliably operate on. Founded in 2024 by Michael Manapat (former CTO of Notion and Head of Applied ML at Stripe) and Yibo Ling (former Chief Business Officer of Binance), the company operates under Emergence Capital's "Agentic Software" thesis with the positioning "You built your firm's edge. Compound it with AI." As of this enrichment pass Rowspace publishes only a marketing website (www.rowspace.ai) and has no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures verified company identity and a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Santa Cruz Operation
providers.description: Santa Cruz Operation (SCO) was an American software company founded in 1979 in Santa Cruz, California, best known for its Unix operating systems for Intel x86 hardware — Xenix (developed with Microsoft), SCO UNIX, SCO OpenServer, and UnixWare. The company later reorganized as Tarantella, Inc. and The SCO Group, which became widely known for the SCO v. IBM Linux litigation beginning in 2003. The SCO Group filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2007, and its Unix product assets were subsequently sold to UnXis, later renamed Xinuos. The historic Santa Cruz Operation is defunct and operates no modern developer platform or public API; this record is retained for network completeness.

providers.name: Storability
providers.description: Storability Software was an enterprise storage resource management (SRM) company founded in 2000 and headquartered in Southborough, Massachusetts. It built software to simplify and centralize the management of complex, multi-site, multi-vendor storage infrastructures, raising roughly $67M from investors including Battery Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Madison Dearborn Partners. The company was acquired by Storage Technology Corporation (StorageTek) on October 11, 2004, and no longer operates as an independent entity. It has no surviving website, developer portal, or public API surface.

providers.name: SynQuest
providers.description: SynQuest, Inc. (formerly Nasdaq: SYNQ) was an Atlanta, Georgia based supply-chain planning and logistics software company that provided e-business solutions to optimize the financial and operational performance of the supply chain, including transportation, distribution, and inventory planning and simulation for customers such as Ford Motor Company. SynQuest reverse-merged with Viewlocity, Inc. in November 2002 (Viewlocity merged into SynQuest as the surviving entity) and was delisted from the Nasdaq SmallCap Market shortly after. Insight Partners (formerly Insight Venture Partners) was an early investor, which is why the company appears in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead. The company is inactive today and publishes no live website, developer portal, or public API surface; enrichment searches found only historical SEC filings and press coverage.

providers.name: Systems Center
providers.description: Systems Center, Inc. was a mainframe and enterprise systems-management software vendor best known for the NetMaster network-management product line. The company was acquired by Sterling Software of Dallas in a 1993 deal (approximately $185M), after which NetMaster was folded into Sterling's data-communications portfolio and rebranded (Connect:Direct lineage); Sterling Software was itself acquired by Computer Associates in 2000. Systems Center was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. An enrichment pass (2026-07-21) searched for any live website, developer portal, or API surface and found none: the company is defunct with no independent public presence, so no API artifacts apply.

providers.name: Vantus
providers.description: Vantus is a stub surfaced from the Mayfield portfolio page whose permalink slug is "vantus" but whose actual company is Vantive Corporation, a historic Mayfield "Milestone" enterprise investment described by Mayfield as call center software leaders. Vantive provided customer relationship management (CRM) software and existed as an independent corporation until its merger with PeopleSoft in 1999; PeopleSoft was later acquired by Oracle and the Vantive brand no longer exists. There is no current company website or API surface to enrich. Unrelated live domains (vantus.com, Vantus Medical Systems; vantus.io, a Spanish AI automation consultancy) are different companies and are intentionally not linked here.

providers.name: Versant
providers.description: Versant Corporation was an American software company that built specialized object and NoSQL data-management systems, notably the Versant Object Database (VOD) and the FastObjects embeddable object database. Its persistence technology was accessed through language-native C++, Java (JDO/JPA-style) and .NET APIs rather than a REST web API, and was deployed across telecommunications, energy, financial services, transportation, manufacturing and defense. Backed by Trinity Ventures, Versant IPO'd on NASDAQ (VSNT) in July 1996 and was acquired by Actian Corporation in December 2012; the product line continues today as the Actian NoSQL Object Database.

providers.name: Virsa Systems
providers.description: Virsa Systems was a governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) software company founded in 1996 that specialized in helping enterprises meet regulatory requirements such as Sarbanes-Oxley by embedding automated control design, testing, and enforcement directly into their business processes, notably around SAP access controls and segregation-of-duties. Lightspeed Venture Partners invested in the company at an early stage in 2004, and Virsa Systems was acquired by SAP in 2006, becoming the foundation of what is now SAP GRC / SAP Access Control. It no longer operates as an independent company and maintains no separate website, developer portal, or public API. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical/portfolio record; there is no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: WallData
providers.description: WallData (Wall Data Inc.) was a Kirkland, Washington host-connectivity software company, best known for its RUMBA family of PC-to-mainframe and AS/400 terminal-emulation and SNA-to-TCP/IP connectivity products. A Trinity Ventures portfolio company that reached an IPO exit, Wall Data was acquired by NetManage in 1999; the RUMBA product line later passed to Micro Focus and now sits under OpenText. The company is defunct and publishes no current developer portal, documentation, or public API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical VC-portfolio record.

providers.name: Waveset
providers.description: Waveset Technologies was a privately held identity-management software vendor based in Austin, Texas, and an early portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. Its flagship product, Lighthouse, automated user provisioning, password management, and identity brokering to govern access to enterprise systems and data. Sun Microsystems announced its acquisition of Waveset in 2003 and completed it in December 2003; the Lighthouse technology became the basis of Sun Identity Manager and was later carried into Oracle's identity portfolio. Waveset has not existed as an independent company since the acquisition and publishes no active website, developer portal, or API surface today.

providers.name: XELUS
providers.description: Xelus was a service parts planning and optimization software company founded in 1972 and headquartered in Fairport, New York, providing inventory management and supply chain solutions for the telecommunications, aerospace and defense, and high-tech industries. An Insight Venture Partners portfolio company, Xelus was acquired by Click Commerce on May 27, 2005, and no longer operates independently. Its website (xelus.com) is defunct and the company publishes no public API surface, developer portal, SDKs, or packages.

providers.name: Alphabet
providers.description: The parent company of Google and one of the world's most valuable corporations. Operates the dominant search engine, Android mobile OS, YouTube, Google Cloud, and Waymo autonomous vehicles alongside numerous technology ventures.

providers.name: Kanarys
providers.description: Kanarys, Inc. was a Dallas, Texas workforce-analytics company founded in 2018 by Mandy Price, Star Carter and Bennie King. Its SaaS platform combined employee experience surveys, demographic and cultural data, anonymous employee reviews and peer benchmarking to give enterprise HR and diversity leaders analytics on workplace inclusion. Integration with customer HRIS, ATS and payroll systems was delivered as managed, per-customer connectors run by Kanarys staff rather than as a self-serve public API, and the company never published a developer portal, an OpenAPI or any other machine-readable contract. Kanarys raised a $5M Series A, counted 7-Eleven and Yum! Brands among its customers, and in mid-2024 sold its intellectual property and name to a special-purpose vehicle formed by a group of former chief diversity officers; co-founder Mandy Price left for the Draper Richards Kaplan Foundation in February 2025. The company now operates no public web surface: kanarys.com served the real site as recently as 22 April 2026 and is a GoDaddy parking lander as of 17 May 2026, and no successor domain resolves.

providers.description: APP Group (renamed Ness Czechia after its acquisition by Ness Digital Engineering) is an enterprise IT services and systems-integration company headquartered in Prague, Czech Republic, with offices in Brno and Ostrava. Operating today as Ness Czech s.r.o., it is one of the most significant SAP providers (SAP Gold Partner) in the Czech Republic and the wider CEE region, delivering system integration, ERP and SAP S/4HANA implementation, business intelligence, data analytics, eGovernment / eHealth registers, core banking, pricing and billing, CRM and portals, IoT, and digital-platform engineering to large enterprises and the public sector. It is not a public API provider: it does not publish a developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a self-serve API program. providers.name: Vineti
providers.description: Vineti was an enterprise software company for cell and gene therapy supply chain management, headquartered in San Francisco and founded in 2016. Its Personalized Therapy Management (PTM) platform — sold as PTM Enterprise and PTM Essentials — orchestrated the patient-centric supply chain behind autologous and allogeneic cell therapies, gene therapies and personalized cancer vaccines: chain of identity, chain of custody, apheresis and manufacturing scheduling, clinical-site workflows, and regulatory reporting. PTM was delivered as a configurable aPaaS on AWS, with HIPAA compliance certified by Avertium and GAMP-aligned validation. Vineti was named a World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer and raised a $35M Series C in 2020. The PTM software was acquired by Johnson & Johnson in 2023 to continue supporting its commercial therapy rollouts and clinical trials, and Vineti ceased to operate as an independent company: vineti.com no longer resolves and the domain now sits on Johnson & Johnson name servers. This profile is retained as a historical record — there is no live API surface to catalog.

providers.name: CES International
providers.description: CES International was a software company founded in 1989 and based in Alpharetta, Georgia, that built real-time software solutions for distribution utilities — including the Centricity operations resource management (ORM) system with outage-management capabilities and an energy delivery management (EDM) suite for network operations — serving utilities on five continents and more than 35 million metered accounts. It was acquired by SPL WorldGroup in May 2004, and SPL WorldGroup was in turn acquired by Oracle in November 2006, where its utilities software became the foundation of the Oracle Utilities global business unit. CES International no longer operates as an independent company: it publishes no developer portal, no documentation, and no API surface, and none of its historical domains resolve to a live company site. This record is retained as a historical / defunct entry in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Pathgather
providers.description: Pathgather was an enterprise Learning Experience Platform (LXP), founded in 2012 and headquartered in New York City, that helped large enterprises curate, share, and track learning content across their existing learning ecosystems. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Techstars, Pathgather (co-founded by CEO Eric Duffy) was one of the companies that established the LXP category before being acquired by Degreed in June 2018; all employees joined Degreed and the standalone product was wound down. Pathgather exposed a REST API in its operating years (a community Python client, tonybaloney/pathgather, remains on PyPI as historical evidence), but the company no longer operates independently: the pathgather.com domain is now parked and publishes no live API, developer portal, or documentation surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired/defunct company record.

providers.name: DWL
providers.description: DWL Inc. was an enterprise software company founded in 1996 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, with significant engineering and operations in Toronto, Ontario. DWL built customer data integration (CDI) middleware — its flagship product, DWL Customer, was a real-time master data hub that consolidated fragmented customer records from across banking, insurance, telecommunications, and retail systems into a single authoritative view, and served that view back to operational applications through a transaction-oriented services layer. Backed by Insight Venture Partners, AGF Investments, Nationwide Mutual Capital, Royal Trust, and Stone Point Capital, DWL was acquired by IBM in August 2005 to fill the CDI gap in IBM's information-management stack. DWL Customer was rebranded IBM WebSphere Customer Center and subsequently folded into IBM InfoSphere Master Data Management. DWL has not operated as an independent company for two decades, never published a public developer program or API, and the dwl.com domain now redirects to ibm.com. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Latitude Communications
providers.description: Latitude Communications, Inc. was a Santa Clara, California enterprise conferencing company, incorporated in April 1993 and venture-backed by Mayfield Fund, Menlo Ventures, Asset Management Associates, and Canaan Ventures (Canaan Partners). It developed, sold, and hosted MeetingPlace, an integrated voice and web conferencing system for geographically dispersed enterprises, first shipped commercially in December 1994 and sold to more than 430 enterprise customers by the end of 2002, including Aetna, Cisco, Credit Suisse First Boston, Fidelity Investments, Lockheed Martin, Oracle, and the U.S. Federal Reserve Bank. The company IPO'd on the Nasdaq National Market under the symbol LATD at $12.00 per share in May 1999 and reported revenue of $43.4 million in 2000, $33.9 million in 2001, and $40.5 million in 2002. Cisco Systems acquired Latitude in a cash merger at $3.95 per share, completed in late 2003; Latitude filed a Form 15 terminating its SEC registration on 2004-01-13, and MeetingPlace was absorbed into Cisco's conferencing line as Cisco Unified MeetingPlace. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and never published a public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface — its 10-K describes only internally developed APIs used to integrate MeetingPlace with web, e-mail, and fax servers. This profile is retained as a historical record of the Canaan Partners portfolio and is not an active API provider.
