providers.name: Benchmark
providers.description: Benchmark is an American early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1995 by Bob Kagle, Bruce Dunlevie, Andy Rachleff, Kevin Harvey, and Val Vaden, and headquartered at 140 New Montgomery Street in San Francisco, California (with a second office in Woodside). Benchmark is known for its distinctive equal partnership structure, where a small number of general partners share ownership and carry equally with no junior/senior hierarchy and no managing partner. The firm concentrates on leading first institutional rounds — typically Series A — and historically kept fund sizes small (around $425M) with a focus on consumer, marketplaces, social, open source, developer tools, infrastructure, enterprise software, fintech, crypto, and artificial intelligence. Benchmark has backed transformational companies including eBay, Uber, Twitter, Instagram, Snap, Dropbox, Discord, Docker, Zendesk, Confluent, Elastic, New Relic, Asana, Amplitude, Nextdoor, Stitch Fix, Yelp, OpenTable, Zillow, Red Hat, Airtable, Benchling, Cockroach Labs, Chainalysis, HackerOne, Contentful, Modern Treasury, Stytch, and, more recently, AI-native companies such as LangChain, Cerebras, MindsDB, Lovable, Legora, Gumloop, and Starcloud. In 2026 Benchmark broke with tradition to raise roughly $2B across two new vehicles, including its first-ever dedicated later-stage growth fund. This profile tracks Benchmark's identity and its portfolio graph across the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bonfire Ventures
providers.description: Bonfire Ventures is a Los Angeles-based, seed-stage venture capital firm co-founded by Mark Mullen and Jim Andelman that invests exclusively in business-to-business (B2B) software companies, with a current focus on AI-native B2B founders. The firm runs a low-volume, high-conviction, high-support model — backing roughly 10 to 12 new companies a year, leading approximately 95% of the rounds it participates in and taking board seats — and positions itself as "AI-native too," operating an in-house AI system called Bonnie to source and support founders. Bonfire reports more than $18B in cumulative exit value across its history, with notable outcomes including TaxJar (acquired by Stripe), MNTN (IPO), The Trade Desk, Scopely, Moat (acquired by Oracle), and Comparably (acquired by ZoomInfo). It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Foundry Group and enriched from the firm's public site.

providers.name: Costanoa Ventures
providers.description: Costanoa Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in June 2012 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with an additional office in San Francisco. Costanoa invests primarily at the Seed and Series A stages, writing checks of roughly $1M to $10M and taking concentrated 10-15% ownership across about 35 companies per fund. The firm's thesis is to fill the "missing middle" of early-stage venture by providing unusually hands-on, operator-led support to founders building applied AI, AI and data infrastructure, cybersecurity, national security / defense tech, fintech, and enterprise software companies. Costanoa was founded by Greg Sands (an early Netscape product manager) and manages roughly $2.8B in assets. In September 2024 it closed an oversubscribed Fund V at $275M alongside Opportunity Fund III at $119M, doubling down on AI-enabled B2B technology. Portfolio companies include Alation, Cyberhaven, Quizlet, PayNearMe, Auterion, Vannevar Labs, Kepler Communications, and Muon Space.

providers.name: Emergence Capital
providers.description: Emergence Capital is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2003 and headquartered in San Francisco, California, focused exclusively on early-stage B2B / enterprise software. Its founding thesis — that business software would move to the cloud — produced some of the defining SaaS bets of the era, including a contrarian 2003 investment in Salesforce and being the sole venture backer of Veeva's 2008 Series A. The firm runs a deliberately high-conviction, low-volume model in which each partner makes roughly one investment per year, enabling deep engagement with every founder. Its current thesis centers on "AI-native services" — companies that sell outcomes rather than software subscriptions, whose service margins improve as AI models improve — alongside AI infrastructure, physical-world AI, and horizontal and vertical SaaS. Emergence closed Fund VII at $1B in March 2025 (its largest fund, following Fund VI at $575M in 2021), has deployed less than $2.5B to generate $9B+ in realized returns, and its portfolio companies are collectively worth over $450B. Notable investments include Salesforce, Zoom, Veeva, Box, Bill.com, Gusto, Doximity, and Ironclad. Reported outcomes: 90%+ of early-stage investments raised successful follow-ons, 20%+ surpassed a $1B valuation, and 10%+ went public.

providers.name: First Round Capital
providers.description: First Round Capital is a seed-stage venture capital firm founded in 2004 by Josh Kopelman and Howard Morgan, headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York and Philadelphia. First Round invests almost exclusively at the earliest stages of company creation, typically writing lead checks in the $750K to $4M range, and partners (many of them former founders) work side-by-side with companies through their first few years. The firm is a generalist that seeks contrarian insight into how markets work, with concentration in enterprise software, AI, fintech, healthcare, hardware, and consumer. Since founding it has backed 500+ startups and was the first institutional investor in Uber; its portfolio includes Notion, Roblox, Square, Looker, Upstart, Verkada, Warby Parker, Flatiron Health, and Clay. First Round also runs The Review, a widely read operator-focused editorial publication, and self-reports roughly $2.5B in assets under management.

providers.name: Greylock Partners
providers.description: Greylock Partners is one of the oldest and best-known venture capital firms in the United States, founded in 1965 in Cambridge, Massachusetts and headquartered in Menlo Park, California. Greylock is an early-stage-focused firm that partners with founders at the pre-seed, seed, and Series A stages, deploying the majority of its capital as a first check and continuing to back companies through Series B and beyond. The firm reports over $3.5 billion in committed capital under management. Greylock invests across enterprise and consumer software with an explicitly AI-first thesis, concentrating on applications, infrastructure, cybersecurity, fintech, consumer, and deep tech. Its portfolio and alumni network includes category-defining companies such as LinkedIn, Facebook, Airbnb, Workday, Palo Alto Networks, Cloudera, Coinbase, Figma, Discord, and Anthropic. Partners include Reid Hoffman, Asheem Chandna, Saam Motamedi, Jerry Chen, David Sze, and Mike Duboe.

providers.name: ICONIQ Capital
providers.description: ICONIQ Capital is a global investment firm founded in December 2011 by Divesh Makan, Michael Anders, and Chad Boeding, headquartered in San Francisco, California with offices in Palo Alto, New York, London, and Singapore. ICONIQ operates as a hybrid family office and multi-strategy investment firm serving ultra-high-net-worth technology entrepreneurs, executives, and their families, and reports over $100B in assets under management across investment management, real assets, venture and growth, and impact strategies. Its venture arm, ICONIQ Growth, partners with founders from inception through IPO and beyond, backing category-leading technology companies across enterprise software, infrastructure, data, developer tools, fintech, security, healthcare IT, and — since 2023 — artificial intelligence as a core theme. ICONIQ Growth has invested in 140+ companies and produced notable outcomes including Snowflake, Airbnb, GitLab, HashiCorp, Datadog, Docusign, Adyen, Uber, Zoom, and Procore, alongside active AI positions in Anthropic, OpenAI, Writer, Glean, ElevenLabs, and Sierra.

providers.name: Institutional Venture Partners
providers.description: Institutional Venture Partners (IVP) is a later-stage venture capital and growth equity firm founded in 1980 by Reid Dennis and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with offices in San Francisco and London. One of the oldest venture firms in Silicon Valley, IVP concentrates on the fastest-growing, most prominent late-stage and growth-stage technology companies each year, typically writing checks in the $10M to $100M range and taking a long-term view toward value creation. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, fintech, cybersecurity, developer tools and cloud infrastructure, data and AI, consumer internet, media, gaming, and healthcare. Across roughly 45 years and 18 funds (Fund XVIII closed at $1.6B in 2024) IVP has backed more than 400 companies and seen 135+ IPOs, with roughly $7B–$8B in assets under management. Notable investments and exits include Netflix, Twitter, Snap, Coinbase, Dropbox, GitHub, Slack, Datadog, CrowdStrike, HashiCorp, UiPath, Robinhood, Klarna, Wise, Figma, Grammarly, Rubrik, Discord, Anthropic, Perplexity, and DeepL.

providers.name: Kleiner Perkins
providers.description: Kleiner Perkins is one of Silicon Valley's oldest and most storied venture capital firms, founded in 1972 by Eugene Kleiner and Tom Perkins and headquartered on Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, California, with additional offices in San Francisco and Shanghai. Across more than five decades and 21 venture funds plus 6 growth funds, the firm has invested over $10 billion and backed more than 900 ventures, including foundational companies such as Amazon, Google, Genentech, Electronic Arts, Juniper Networks, Intuit, Spotify, Figma, Robinhood, DoorDash, Duolingo and Databricks. Kleiner Perkins partners with founders from inception through IPO and beyond across early and growth stages, with seed rounds averaging roughly $4-5M and Series A rounds around $17-18M. In 2026 the firm announced its twenty-second venture fund, KP22, a $1B early-stage fund, alongside $2.5B in new growth funds. Current investment focus centers on artificial intelligence and AI safety, enterprise software, developer tools and infrastructure, healthcare and biotech, fintech, hardtech and autonomous systems, and cybersecurity, with a thesis that the right idea, team and partners can create an entirely new industry.

providers.name: Lightspeed Venture Partners
providers.description: Lightspeed Venture Partners is a global, multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 2000 by Barry Eggers, Christopher Schaepe, Ravi Mhatre, and Peter Nieh, and headquartered in Menlo Park, California. Lightspeed invests from seed through Series F and beyond, backing bold builders across artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, cloud and enterprise infrastructure, developer tools, fintech, consumer, gaming, and healthcare/biotech. The firm operates as a single global team across roughly a dozen offices in the United States, Europe, Israel, India, and Southeast Asia, with U.S./Europe/Israel run by Lightspeed Management Company (LSVP) and India/Southeast Asia by Lightspeed India Partners (LSIP). Lightspeed reports managing on the order of $25B+ (up to $40B+ by some self-reported figures) across the Lightspeed platform. Notable investments and exits include Anthropic, Mistral AI, ElevenLabs, Wiz, Rubrik, Cato Networks, Stripe, Affirm, Snap, Nutanix, MuleSoft, AppDynamics, Nest, Grafana, ngrok, Faire, and Navan.

providers.name: Mayfield Fund
providers.description: Mayfield Fund is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1969 and headquartered on Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, California, with a presence in Mumbai, India. One of the oldest continuously active Silicon Valley firms, Mayfield describes itself as "people first, from inception" and reports that roughly 70% of its investments begin at company inception, positioning it as the first institutional investor for early-stage founders. The firm invests primarily at the Seed, Series A, and Series B stages across artificial intelligence, enterprise software, cloud and cybersecurity infrastructure, semiconductors, consumer and social commerce, and human and planetary health. Mayfield reports approximately $3B in assets under management (and states it has committed $3B to AI investments), has backed more than 550 companies over its history, and counts 120+ IPOs and 225+ M&A exits including Genentech, Lyft, HashiCorp, Poshmark, Marketo, Couchbase, SolarCity, Intuitive Surgical, and Compaq. In 2023 the firm raised $955M across two new funds dedicated to early-stage investing.

providers.name: New Enterprise Associates
providers.description: New Enterprise Associates (NEA) is one of the world's largest and longest-running venture capital firms, founded in 1977 by Dick Kramlich, Chuck Newhall, and Frank Bonsal. Headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with offices in Timonium (Maryland), New York, and London, NEA invests across the full company lifecycle — "from idea to IPO" — spanning seed, Series A, and later growth rounds. The firm has raised over $27 billion in committed capital (as of December 31, 2024) and organizes into specialized practice groups across two core sectors: technology (enterprise software, consumer, fintech, AI, infrastructure) and healthcare (biopharma, life sciences, digital health, and medical devices). NEA is known for an active, hands-on partnership model and long-term support of category-defining companies, with a portfolio that has produced many notable IPOs and acquisitions including Cloudflare, MongoDB, Robinhood, Coursera, Databricks, Plaid, and Tempus.

providers.name: Sapphire Ventures
providers.description: Sapphire Ventures is a global software venture capital firm that partners with expansion-stage enterprise technology companies it believes can become category leaders. Originally founded in 1996 as the venture arm of SAP, the firm spun out as an independent company in 2011 and rebranded to Sapphire Ventures in 2014. Sapphire manages over $10 billion in assets under management and typically invests Series B through IPO, with check sizes commonly ranging from roughly $2M to $30M, while its Sapphire Sport and Sapphire Partners arms address early-stage sports/media and fund investing respectively. The firm concentrates on Enterprise AI and B2B software, including data and analytics, cybersecurity, DevOps and developer tools, fintech, health tech, and vertical SaaS. Headquartered in Austin, Texas, with offices in San Francisco, Menlo Park, New York, and London, Sapphire backs companies of consequence and supports them with a large platform team that drives executive talent and customer introductions. The portfolio spans 30+ IPOs and 80+ exits including DocuSign, Square, Wise, monday.com, JFrog, Auth0, MuleSoft, and LinkedIn.

providers.name: Shasta Ventures
providers.description: Shasta Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2004 and based in Silicon Valley (Portola Valley / Menlo Park, on and around Sand Hill Road, California). Founded by Rob Coneybeer and Ravi Mohan (with Tod Francis and Jason Pressman among its long-tenured Managing Directors), the firm invests primarily at the Series A stage in United States technology startups, typically leading rounds and taking board seats. Shasta has roughly $1.3B under management across multiple funds (Fund II $250M, Fund III $265M, Fund IV $300M) and a 20-year track record. Its thesis centers on enterprise software / SaaS, cybersecurity, developer tools and infrastructure, data intelligence, camera / computer vision, and consumer subscription products, pairing capital with operational support (Shasta Elevate) for technical founders. Notable investments include Anaplan, Zuora, Nest, Nextdoor, Apptio, Eero, Sendbird, Tonal, Lattice, Highspot, SentinelOne and Turo, with 12 unicorns, multiple IPOs and dozens of acquisitions across its history.

providers.name: SoftBank Vision Fund
providers.description: SoftBank Vision Fund (managed by SoftBank Investment Advisers) is one of the world's largest technology-focused investment funds, launched in May 2017 by SoftBank Group and anchored by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia. Now operating across two funds (SVF1 and SVF2) with combined assets under management reported at roughly $150B+, the fund pursues Masayoshi Son's long "AI economy" thesis, backing high-growth companies across the AI stack: hardware and semiconductors, the software infrastructure to gather, process and deploy data, and the applications built on top of it. It typically writes large late-stage growth checks (Series C/D and beyond, often $100M to several billion) into 300+ companies worldwide, spanning enterprise software, consumer internet, health tech, fintech, logistics, transportation, frontier tech, edtech and proptech across the Americas, EMEA and Asia. Headquartered in London, with major offices in the US and Asia, its portfolio includes many unicorns and household names such as Arm, ByteDance, and Aurora.

providers.name: Spark Capital
providers.description: Spark Capital is a multi-stage venture capital firm founded in 2005 by Paul Conway, Santo Politi, Todd Dagres, and Bijan Sabet, with offices in San Francisco, New York, and Boston. Spark is a generalist firm that partners with founders from seed through growth across consumer internet, enterprise software, artificial intelligence, gaming, crypto, fintech, infrastructure, hardware and semiconductors, life sciences, aerospace, and the future of work. The firm invests from a family of early-stage funds (most recently a $700M fund in 2024) and dedicated growth funds (most recently a $1.4B fund in 2024), and press reports have placed its assets under management in the range of $12-15 billion. Spark first became widely known for leading Twitter's Series B in 2008 and has since backed a run of defining companies including Slack, Discord, Snap, Coinbase, Affirm, Plaid, Cruise, Oculus, Scale AI, Ramp, Deel, and Anthropic, whose Series C investment the firm turned into one of venture's largest recent markups. Spark rebranded in 2020 with design studio Pentagram around its distinctive dog-themed identity, and publishes a curated set of portfolio companies rather than a full list.

providers.name: Threshold Ventures
providers.description: Threshold Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm based in Menlo Park, California that backs founder-led technology companies at the threshold of breakout growth. Threshold is the 2019 rebrand of Draper Fisher Jurvetson (DFJ), the storied Sand Hill Road firm founded in 1985; managing partners Emily Melton and Josh Stein spun the venture practice into an independent, focused fund. Threshold pursues a high-conviction strategy, concentrating on a small number of Series A and Series B investments and partnering hands-on with founders for the long term, frequently holding board seats through IPO and beyond. The firm invests across enterprise software and SaaS, developer tools and infrastructure, fintech, digital health and healthcare, and AI. Its portfolio has produced 10 unicorns, 3 IPOs, and 17 acquisitions, and includes Box, Twilio, Redfin, Remitly, Doximity, Rippling, LaunchDarkly, Livongo, and Talkdesk. Threshold has invested in roughly 87 companies and raised a ~$250M fund following the rebrand.

providers.name: Trinity Ventures
providers.description: Trinity Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1986 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, with more than three decades of history backing mission-driven entrepreneurs across technology and consumer markets. The firm takes a deliberately personal, low-capital-to-partner approach to early-stage investing, positioning itself as "the call you want to make, not the call you have to make" and emphasizing intellectual candor and lasting founder relationships. Trinity invests primarily at seed, Series A and Series B, with checks generally ranging from roughly $1 million to $15 million and averaging around $5 million. Its focus spans enterprise software and cloud infrastructure, developer tools, fintech, digital media and marketing technology, consumer products and services, healthcare, and artificial intelligence. Over nine funds the firm has managed on the order of $1.3 billion in assets and produced a track record that includes multiple unicorns, IPOs and roughly 130 acquisitions. Notable investments include Starbucks, New Relic, Auth0, Turo, Care.com, Zulily, Blue Nile, Aruba Networks, Infoblox, Cohesity, Outreach, InfluxData, Contentful and Docker. Trinity invests primarily in the United States.

providers.name: Wing Venture Capital
providers.description: Wing Venture Capital is an early-stage venture firm founded in 2013 by Peter Wagner and Gaurav Garg (both former partners at Sequoia Capital and Accel) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. Wing invests at the stealth, seed, and Series A stages in companies building the "AI-first" technology stack, and positions itself as a long-term company builder rather than a passive investor. Its thesis spans autonomous applications, AI and machine learning, data platforms and infrastructure, product-led growth (PLG), Web3, and bio x data. Wing raised its fourth flagship fund, Wing Four, a $600M early-stage vehicle, in 2023. Notable outcomes across its portfolio include Snowflake, Cohesity, Gong, Shape Security, and Deepgram, and it operates a Founder Success Platform plus the ET30 (Enterprise Tech 30) research program led by its research team.
